#2757. Art Rooney II expresses support for Mike McCarthy, calls Aaron Rodgers not a "good teammate"

After Wednesday’s unprecedented chaos, it had to happen. And it did.

Steelers owner Art Rooney II has addressed the events that resulted in the benching and then the firing of quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

“A change had to be made, and I certainly agree with the change and the way it was handled,” Rooney told Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette in a Thursday interview.

The change was sparked by the notion that Rodgers gave coach Mike McCarthy an ultimatum: “Either let me call all the plays or just release me.” Instead, McCarthy benched him.

It went to the next level when, as many expected, Rodgers scurried to the McAfee show to take shots at McCarthy for missing meetings, showing up late to meetings, and falling asleep in meetings — among other things, including the ultra-embarrassing “1-2-3 Packers!” moment from halftime of Sunday’s loss to the Eagles.

“There’s maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload,” Rooney said. “He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don’t do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that’s for sure. . . .

“In general, I think, historically, what’s in the locker room stays in the locker room. That’s the way it’s always been. That’s the way it should be as far as I’m concerned.”

Rooney also confirmed that the team supports McCarthy, despite Rodgers’s rant and reports confirming the facts underpinning the petty delivery of them.

“I just want to say that I have 100 [percent] confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney told Dulac. “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.”

Rooney also was asked whether Rodgers raised with the owner supposed concerns about McCarthy’s health.

“Nothing,” Rooney said. “Mike’s as healthy as the rest of us. Health was not an issue. I’m not sure where that part comes [from].”

Rooney also addressed something that has been largely overlooked during the fast-moving drama: Rodgers’s subpar performance.

“The sad thing is Mike took some of the bullets for Aaron in terms of some of the plays that were called, particularly in the red-zone troubles that we had,” Rooney said. “Mike took some of the bullets for things that were going wrong down there. He tried to protect him, and it just wasn’t working.”

They should have known it wouldn’t work between Rodgers and McCarthy. It’s still unclear why either one of them thought it would. McCarthy shouldn’t have wanted a reunion with Rodgers. And Rodgers shouldn’t have wanted a second act with McCarthy.

Then again, it’s not as if Rodgers had many choices. In 2025, he had few takers. In 2026, he had fewer. If he was going to ensure that his final NFL throw wasn’t a pick-six by playing another year, Pittsburgh wasn’t just the best place.

#2754. St. Louis Blues’ Injury Troubles Create an Intriguing Opportunity

Just when it looked like the St. Louis Blues were starting to correct course, they now need to find a way to stay on track while battling through injuries to some of their key players. Pavel Buchnevich and Jimmy Snuggerud are both day-to-day with upper-body injuries, while Connor McMichael and Brandon Carlo are on injured reserve as they try to recover from lower-body injuries.

The Blues recalled Adam Jiricek to try to fill the void left by Carlo, but the bigger concern is up front. They lost their most consistent offensive performer this season in Snuggerud, one of their key offseason acquisitions in McMichael, and a player who was starting to look like his former self in Buchnevich. The Blues are going to need players to step up, and every player on their new-look second line of Mason McTavish, Dalibor Dvorsky, and Otto Stenberg has something to prove.

McTavish went looking for a situation where he could become a bigger part of a team, and the Blues came knocking, believing he could be their second-line center of the future. McTavish looked the part through his first 10 games, scoring six goals and adding four assists, but since then, he has hit a bit of a lull. He has just three goals and two assists in his last 15 games, and if the Blues want to stay in the playoff hunt, they are going to need him to look like the player we saw at the start of the season.

When the Blues acquired McTavish from the Anaheim Ducks, the vision was that he would form a one-two punch down the middle with Robert Thomas. They need him to be the engine that makes the line work. He does not need to be the one scoring all the goals or creating all the plays for his teammates, but it is the little things he does that can make the difference. Strong forechecking, winning battles along the boards, and crashing the net are all things he is capable of doing to make life a little easier for Dvorsky and Stenberg.

Despite the downtick in production over the last 15 games, he has shown some signs of turning it around, with three of his five points during this stretch coming in the last three games. His improved play is going to have to continue, especially with two linemates who are still trying to find their footing in the NHL.

Both Dvorsky and Stenberg have shown flashes of what they are capable of but have yet to do so consistently. However, the situation is a little bit different for the 10th and 25th overall picks in the 2023 NHL Draft.

Coming into the season, the hope was that Dvorsky could take that next step in his development and become a real contributor. His performance as a rookie left much to be desired, with 12 goals and nine assists in 71 games, but he has shown in the AHL that he has the talent to be an effective player at the top level. He has played lower in the lineup and has seen his ice time fluctuate, but he now has a chance to show what he is capable of in an expanded role.

For Stenberg, the challenge is establishing himself as an everyday NHL player. Stenberg played in 32 games with the Blues last season, and coming into training camp, the next step for him was making the team. That did not happen, as Stenberg started the season with the Springfield Thunderbirds. He was recalled in October, played in three games, then was sent back to Springfield. However, with the Blues dealing with injuries, he was recalled again. He is not just in the lineup. He is playing in their top six, giving him his best opportunity yet to succeed and show he belongs in the NHL.

The Blues' offense has been on a roll as of late, scoring 28 goals in their last five games, and if they want to keep that momentum going, they are going to need McTavish, Dvorsky, and Stenberg to contribute offensively. For McTavish, it is about playing up to expectations, and for Dvorsky and Stenberg, it is about taking advantage of the opportunity they are getting.

#2752. How the Knicks can advance in the NBA Cup

After the Knicks' valiant comeback effort at Gainbridge Fieldhouse came up empty on November 13, they fell to 6-6 on the season and 0-2 in NBA Cup play. After an incredible run the year prior to claim the organization's first trophy of any kind in 27 years (foreshadowing), they seemed fated to become the third consecutive NBA Cup champion to be bounced in the group stage.

Yet, one six-game winning streak and an incredible fourth quarter in a Cup game against the Cavs later, and the Knicks are mathematically alive heading into Black Friday against Giannis Antetokounmpo and the red-hot Miami Heat.

Now, after winning the Treble last year, experiencing the fatigue from last year's Cup run that led to the 2-9 stretch from hell, and, you know, defending a real championship, a tournament that already had limited interest from Knicks fans seems to have the opposite intended effect, to the point where it might be beneficial to miss the knockout round altogether.

But the Knicks are currently the only team to have never been grouped in Cup play, and since these games count toward the team's 82-game record, there's plenty to play for as the Knicks look to defend the first of their three trophies.

Here's a look at the current standings in East Group B and the East's wild card, both of which are still in play:

The simplest path is to win the group, which simply requires two things:

Knicks to beat the Heat by 7 points in regulation

What helps the Knicks here is their point differential. They lost the games to Philly and Indiana by five and two points respectively, which allowed their 19-point win over Cleveland to put them in a decent spot.

Winning an NBA game by seven is the easy part; relying on an injured and struggling Pacers team to defeat the No. 1 seed in the East is another. Now, the Sixers look like a paper tiger with their clutch reliance (their Cup PD is negative because of this), but this reads like a game that would be a blowout.

The current injury report has Jaylen Brown out with hamstring management and Joel Embiid questionable with an illness for the Sixers, while Tyrese Haliburton, Ben Sheppard, and Johnny Furphy are still out for Indiana. TJ McConnell, Larry Nance Jr., and Kelly Oubre Jr. are questionable.

If the Sixers win, they clinch Group B. If they lose, the Knicks will get a shot at being the first 2-loss NBA Cup group winner in an unlikely five-way tie.

In the event of a Sixers win, things get a lot more complicated.

First of all, the Knicks would need there to be zero 3-1 non-group winners for obvious reasons. That means they'll need losses from the Hawks, Pistons, and Raptors. Toronto already has a lower point differential, so margin wouldn't matter there.

Margin would matter with the other two. The Hawks are at +21 and the Pistons are at +31, so the Knicks are going to need to win and win by a lot to guarantee they get in.

The simplest path to a wild card berth in the event of a Sixers win looks like this:

The margin of victory would likely not need to be that big, as the more the Pistons and Hawks lose by, the more it knocks that down. The absolute minimum the Knicks would have to win by is seven to pass the Heat in point differential, but to only have to win by that much, they'd need the Bucks to win by 13 and the Celtics to win by 3.

Which brings the difficulty aspect. You're asking two of the worst teams in the league to win games against significantly better teams, one of which is a matchup between a 2-win Bucks team and the reigning No. 1 seed. That's probably not happening.

Also, there is the spoiler aspect that could theoretically damage both of these scenarios. If the Pacers (-27 PD) or Nets (-11 PD) win by such ridiculous margins, they would have a chance to steal a spot in the knockout round.

Now, personally, a Hali-less Pacers team winning by damn near 50 or the Nets beating the Raptors by 30+ would be pretty stunning, but we're already asking for stunning things to happen to get this far.

In layman's terms, a fourth consecutive trip to the knockout round is still unlikely, but possible.

It'll make for a fun night of scoreboard watching, that's for sure.

#2751. Kalshi daily volume of ‘perps’ trading begins to top its prediction markets

Kalshi is known for its prediction markets across sports, politics and culture.

But now, for the first time, perpetual futures, Kalshi's second financial product, has surpassed the notional trading volume of its event contracts on consecutive days.

On Thursday, perpetual futures — commonly known as "perps" — on Kalshi saw $3.4 billion in notional volume as artificial intelligence laboratory Anthropic stock debuted on public markets while the rest of the market sold off. That exceeded about $3 billion in notional volume for Kalshi's prediction markets on the same day.

Perps are futures-style contracts where there is no expiration and traders do not need to own the underlying asset. Contracts instead continuously track the price of an asset, with funding payments to keep the contract price aligned with that of the market. Funding payments are made periodically between holders of short or long positions.

Perps trading surpassed event contracts one day in September, but on Friday perps topped prediction markets volume for a second day. Now Kalshi expects that performance to continue as it introduces perps tied to more individual stocks. On Monday, for example, Kalshi launched contracts linked to Anthropic.

Kalshi was the first to debut perps in the U.S. after winning federal regulatory approval in May to list perps tied to cryptocurrencies.

Perps trading volume includes any leverage that speculators acquire along with their trade, while event contracts are fully collateralized — for now.

Since the original launch in May, Kalshi has received approval to introduce perps tied to metals, crude oil, stock indexes and individual stocks.

Offshore perps — those available on exchanges not regulated in the U.S. — generated more than $90 trillion in notional trading volume in 2025, so it's not surprising that the product has grown so rapidly on Kalshi, according to Udesh Jha, chief risk officer at Kalshi Klear, the company's clearing house.

"We're just in very early innings. We're launching products, we're growing the participant base."

Perps were Kalshi's first product to mark its transition from a prediction market-focused platform to a full-blown financial exchange where various assets are traded. Last week, reports said that Kalshi is planning to offer trading on equities on its platform in the coming months.

At the same time, the company's perps product has come under fire. Some incumbent exchanges where futures are traded — which saw their stock prices decline following the approval of U.S. perps — believe the product was improperly approved. CME Group is suing the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the federal derivatives regulator, for approving perps.

Others have simply expressed concerns about the efficiency of the markets. CNBC previously reported that trading volume on Kalshi's most popular perps markets — tied to bitcoin and ether cryptocurrencies — was dramatically greater than open interest, or cash actively in the markets. It's a phenomenon that isn't common with U.S.-regulated traditional futures, nor other offshore perps markets.

Kalshi said at the time it has "zero concerns" about the distinction, and that it appears because less leverage is offered compared to offshore exchanges and there are fewer incentives for traders to park capital on its perps markets.

While Kalshi started with cryptocurrencies, Owen Lau, an analyst at Clear Street, said perps tied to individual stocks likely represent the most promising opportunity for growth in the U.S.

"That's how I foresee the way perps will penetrate further into traditional asset classes," Lau said. "Perps on single stocks and [key performance indicators on individual companies] could change how investors hedge their portfolio or even make a directional bet."

Kalshi's growth has been powered by the fact that right now it's the only exchange that can actively list perps in the U.S., though crypto exchange Coinbase received approval in May to route U.S. users to offshore platforms for trading. That monopoly status, however, will probably prove short lived.

Coinbase has filed to list single-stock perps in the U.S., and President Donald Trump in August said the CFTC is working to bring Hyperliquid — a dominant player in offshore perps activity — to domestic traders.

But Jha at Kalshi isn't worried about the competition.

"What will carry us is ... making sure that we have the right products for the marketplace, making sure we have the right surveillance of the products that we are trading."

Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

#2748. AI debt markets shudder as Nvidia's top 'banker' returns

AI credit markets are shuddering again with Jensen Huang back as CEO of Nvidia.

Fears about the massive debt being taken on to fund the artificial intelligence buildout climbed Tuesday as Wall Street weighed what Huang's return to Nvidia means for its bankrolling of the AI boom.

Huang is considered one of the top financiers, or bankers, in the AI industry, spearheading deals with neoclouds like CoreWeave and other firms to buy chips, backed in some cases by Nvidia guarantees. His return to Nvidia has revived prospects for the company to continue "circular financing" of AI chips and data centers — raising concerns among credit investors.

CoreWeave, which has become the poster child of AI debt concerns, saw its stock sink 13% and the yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 top 17%. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

At the same time, the spread on the neocloud company's five-year credit default swaps jumped 8.5% to over 1,200 basis points. Credit default swaps are insurance against nonpayment and are considered a barometer of perceived risks. Rising CDS spreads mean investors view the debt as riskier.

Huang was reinstated as CEO on Monday after stepping down on Nov. 12 amid allegations of multiple affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. His reinstatement on Monday was cheered by investors, who pushed stocks higher, yields lower and spreads on CDS tighter. However, stocks retreated, bond yields rose and CDS spreads widened on Tuesday.

Ben Emons, founder and chief investment officer at FedWatch Advisors, called it a waning of the "Jensen effect."

The moves suggest "markets see government intervention as 'moral suasion' that carries credit and interest-rate risks," he said.

President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday he "convinced" the board to bring Huang back.

CoreWeave wasn't the only name seeing heightened concerns in CDS spreads. Oracle's five-year CDS spread jumped 7% to 355.68. Even highly rated hyperscalers Meta Platforms and Amazon.com saw spreads widen by more than 2%. Nvidia's CDS added 3.4%.

Larry Holzenthaler, senior portfolio manager for fixed income at Catalyst Funds, believes the drama that unfolded with Huang's return to Nvidia won't necessarily sit well with credit investors.

"A lot of old school credit people are going to look at what kind of materialized there, the administration's involvement in putting him back in, and I think a lot of credit participants are going to step back and tiptoe away from that a bit," he said. "Credit market investors typically don't like that type of drama or uncertainty."

While Nvidia has commitments across the AI ecosystem, it is the neoclouds that have been under the most scrutiny. Many of the companies, which rent out AI computing power and cloud capacity, are highly leveraged and have relied on Nvidia financing to reduce their exposure to the bond market.

With so much riding on Nvidia's funding, Huang's next move is being closely watched.

During his brief absence, chief financial officer Colette Kress said during the company's earnings call that Nvidia would be "rigorously evaluating future investments" and will remain disciplined in how it commits capital.

That suggested Nvidia was going to be more judicious with financing, says Paul Meeks, head of technology research at Freedom Capital Markets.

"That concern should be put to rest with Jensen [Huang] back," he said.

Investor Steve Eisman, of "Big Short" fame and host of "The Real Eisman Playbook" podcast, believes Huang feels emboldened now that he's back in charge.

"[H]e'll double down on the circular financing," Eisman predicted on CNBC's "Squawk Box" Tuesday.

After Huang's departure, Eisman believed that the ecosystem the CEO created by pouring money into AI companies would likely unwind and leave some of the companies in "big trouble."

"Now that he's back, they're not," he said.

Others are not so certain the level of funding will continue.

"Given scrutiny of disclosure around financing and guarantees … we do not expect Mr. Huang's return to bring a quick reversion to broader customer financing," Stifel analyst Ruben Roy said in a note Monday.

Nvidia said on its earnings call that it has $118 billion in guarantees, as of Oct. 25, to back AI projects.

Concerns about the level of debt to fund the AI infrastructure buildout had already taken hold before Huang's departure and reinstatement.

"These issues have not disappeared just because the White House pressured the weak board to reinstate Jensen Huang," said economist David Rosenberg, founder and president of Rosenberg Research.

John Lloyd, global head of multi-sector and corporate credit at Janus Henderson Investors, believes having Huang back at the helm "reaffirms his existing go-to-market strategy." However, the credit market is still taking a cautious look at the neoclouds as it waits for more clarity on long-term supply/demand dynamics.

Still, Lloyd is cautiously positive on CoreWeave, which he owns in portfolios he manages, and noted all the data point to a "pretty healthy environment right now." That includes strong residual values on graphics processing units and spot compute rates, he noted.

"The company is doing everything in its power to execute," he said. "They don't need the high yield market at this time."

In the meantime, investigations into Nvidia and Huang are ramping up. Huang is expected to appear before three House committees next week. Nvidia is conducting an independent investigation into his activities, and California Attorney General Rob Bonta has launched a probe. At the federal level, President Trump said Monday that U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche "has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct."

"There's other shoes to drop," Rosenberg said. "I don't think that the book has been closed on this file."

#2746. Celtics faced with massive NBA Cup opportunity vs. Hawks

Your Boston Celtics have the chance to win their Emirates NBA Cup group for the first time in the competition's young history.

Now, before you angrily scroll to the comments to tell me how you don't care about the Cup and that an NBA championship is the only thing you want to see this team win, take some deep breaths. You're allowed to want to see your team win every competition that they're a part of.

Through their first three Cup games, the Celtics are undefeated with a +68 point differential — 20 points better than San Antonio, who hold the second-highest differential, and over double the Pistons' +31 mark, which is second best in the East.

In short, they're in a good spot entering their Group C finale against the Atlanta Hawks on Friday night.

All they have to do is win and they'll not only win the group, but clinch the best record in the Eastern Conference, an accomplishment that would reward them with home-c0urt advantage through the semifinals.

BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS – OCTOBER 27: Jayson Tatum #0 of the Boston Celtics celebrates with fans after scoring the game winning basket in overtime to defeat the Brooklyn Nets 125-124 at TD Garden on October 27, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images

Home-court is a sneaky perfect prize for the Cs. The team has spent November touring the country like they just dropped a platinum album. We've seen their play sputter a bit, presumably due to their strenous travel schedule. Guaranteeing themselves two extra home games while they try regain a sense of normalcy and routine would be huge.

Even if they lose, which wouldn't be super shocking against a good Hawks team that's riding a four-game winning streak into this one, they've still got the East's Wild Card to fall back on.

The league shared the full list of scenarios that would see Boston move onto the knockout stage. All you need to know is that they'll be fine as long as the avoid a catestrophic loss.

Now, advancing in the Cup is great. Frankly, it's what we all expected when the groups were announced over the summer and Boston's was clearly the weakest in the conference.

More than anything though, this presents the Celtics with an opportunity to lay a foundation for the remainder of the season. The NBA Cup is unique in that there's so little room for error if you actually want to win the thing. When I wrote about the team's chances earlier this month, I joked that it's harder to win the Cup than to win a title because you can really only lose one game if you want to make it all the way.

Some of you lost your minds in the comments and that's okay.

The competition is still an objectively difficult climb, and there's a reason why the Celtics, in one of the franchise's most successful eras in terms of winning percentage, have yet to make a deep run.

Lifting the trophy at Hinkle Fieldhouse next month would mean that this group rose to the challenge of must-win scenarios. Facing adversity and prevailing is objectively going to bring you closer together. Somewhere down the line when things inevitably get tough in the postseason, a Cup win could serve as a reflection point for Boston.

Let's not get too far ahead of ourselves though. Beating the Hawks tonight is the first step towards any of that.

#2745. T.J. Edwards: Fourth down pass to Jahmyr Gibbs a look we saw all week

The Bears had a hard time stopping Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs throughout Thursday’s game in Detroit, so it made sense that the Lions put the ball in Gibbs’s hands on fourth down with just over two minutes left to play.

Gibbs caught a short pass with forward momentum and one player between him and a first down that would have pushed them much closer to a home win. That player was Bears linebacker T.J. Edwards and Edwards was able to corral Gibbs short of the sticks for a tackle that gave them a chance to steal a win with three seconds left on the clock.

After the 39-35 win, Edwards said he “knew it was going to be me” when he saw how the Lions lined up for the play.

“I knew that there’s gonna be a play that we would have to make,” Edwards said, via Kevin Fishbain of TheAthletic.com. “And we made a play when we needed to. I was happy to do it, grateful for it, man. It was a look that we saw all week, and I was able to make it.”

Gibbs picked up 252 yards on Thursday, but Edwards’s recognition and execution meant the few he didn’t get made all the difference.

#2744. Mike Tomlin on current Steelers situation: "It's a dumpster fire"

Many folks in and around football have had opinions about the recent brouhaha between former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and Steelers coach Mike McCarthy. Few have the insight and perspective that former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin brings to the table.

Appearing on NBC’s Chiefs-Bills halftime show on Thanksgiving night, Tomlin shared his thoughts on the situation in a conversation with Mike Tirico. (A portion of it was on the live broadcast; the full interview is here.)

“I had a range of emotions watching those course of events yesterday,” Tomlin told Tirico. “I think the prevailing one is just general sadness. Sad on a micro level, sad on a macro level. And by that, I mean, you know, just from an individual perspective, sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career of the quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, and just on the macro level, whether it’s organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum.

“Those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football. So, just a lot of emotions, but probably more than anything, man, general sadness on a lot of levels.”

Tirico asked Tomlin if he was shocked by Rodgers’s decision to air dirty laundry in a public forum.

“It certainly did,” Tomlin said, “but, you know, and particularly because I know both men involved, certainly had a lot of intimate work and development of relationship with Aaron over the last couple of years, and have known and competed against Mike, you know, respected and appreciated him as a coach for a long time. But I don’t — what I acknowledge is I don’t know them as a collective, the nature of their relationships, and so certainly I was surprised by that.”

Regardless of Rodgers’s conduct on the way out the door, Tomlin explained that Rodgers was viewed favorably by his teammates in 2025.

“He was beloved, and I’m not, you know, over-exaggerating that,” Tomlin said. “He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness to getting to know and understand the Steeler culture, to be engaged with teammates, and particularly from my perspective, I worked with a lot of veteran players over the years and at times they lose a little patience for the process, or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys, et cetera. Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real, natural way. He was a tireless worker regarding the process.

“I called early-morning quarterback meetings on Wednesday and Thursday. He was always early and engaged. Did a heck of a job in terms of engaging and developing, assisting in the development of young players. Specifically, Will Howard was always in that meeting, and, shoot, man, [Rodgers] and I were shoulder-to-shoulder in terms of the development of Will and challenging Will to develop professional habits. And so, you know, it was early and extremely consistent during my time with him, in terms of his willingness to work in those areas, and I think that’s why he’s so beloved in that locker room, as been reported by multiple sources in light of this incident. That is real. The guys in that locker room love and appreciate Aaron Rodgers.”

Had Tomlin gotten any sense that things were so close to breaking down?

“Absolutely none, but it’s a really specific reason why, to be honest with you, man,” Tomlin said. “One of my cultural mantras, when I worked there for the 19 years, is don’t talk to people about your problems unless they can be a component of the solution. Because if you do, it’s counterproductive, and people know where I stand there. And by that I mean if you have a problem with your playing time, don’t talk to your teammate about it. Talk to somebody that can do something about it. That’s problem solving.

“And so everybody understands my posture on some of that stuff, and so although I have really good, fluid communication with many of those guys, particularly, the more veteran guys, they know me and know me well enough to know that I didn’t want to hear about any potential issues, because I’m not a component of the solution. And so although, particularly, like, Cam Heyward, he and I spent a little time together doing his bye week. Man, we had no mention of anything bubbling under the surface, if you will.”

Can McCarthy effectively lead the team, given what Rodgers said?

“You know, it certainly created some challenges and challenges is probably an understatement if all of those things are true,” Tomlin told Tirico. “And certainly the ‘1-2-3 Packers’ is, because he acknowledged that. But his ability to overcome that or inability to overcome that in my opinion is based on relationships and the depth of those relationships and how those guys feel about him, or how those guys buy into what he’s selling. And so, certainly, he’s been there a short period of time. And so it makes you wonder, the level of that challenge. But it’ll be relationship-based, his ability to overcome the things that you mentioned.”

How does Tomlin think the Steelers will fare against the Broncos on Friday?

“Based on my knowledge of the men, particularly the leaders, the longstanding guys, they’ll do a great job of getting hyper-focused on what really matters, and that’s that football game,” Tomlin said. “They’ll use it as a mantra to bring them together. I expect those guys to fight. Now, fight and quality play are two different things. I’m certainly not gonna expect those guys not to fight. I think they’re gonna fight and fight extremely hard. What I’m interested in is quality of play, quality of execution. And those are things that could be impacted by the level of distraction that they had on a short week in particular.”

Tirico then asked Tomlin how he feels, overall, about what has transpired this week.

“I’m upset about it, you know, it’s a dumpster fire,” Tomlin said. “And I don’t say that in a judgmental way. I presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. But it certainly is upsetting, and I’m sure Steeler Nation is upset.”

If owner Art Rooney II calls Tomlin for advice, what would Tomlin say?

“Hey, Mike, that’s a hypothetical, because I know he wouldn’t and, and because I know how he’s trained,” Tomlin said. “You know, Art is a guy that’s not a hedge fund guy that bought a football team. He’s not a, you know, artificial intelligence guy that bought a football team. This is a family business. It’s generational. Any advice or thought process in that way, I imagine he just says, ‘What would my dad do?’ Or, ‘What would my grandfather do?’ Their mode of operation is time tested, it’s generational. And so, I doubt, very, very seriously, that he called anyone for outside advice.”

Finally, Tirico asked whether Tomlin believes Rodgers will get another NFL opportunity this season, if he wants one.

“There’s certainly a possibility for that,” Tomlin said. “And I just say that based on the 19 years that I held the position that I held. It’s a 32-team league. All it takes is one. Over time, I’ve laughed and watched that people talk about, you know, ‘No, that could never happen.’ In a 32-team league, when everybody is highly competitive and there’s some real challenges, particularly as you get to this portion of the journey from a player availability standpoint, there’s certainly a possibility if he desires that he could play again, because all it takes is one suitor.”

Having cleared waivers, Rodgers is available to that one suitor, if/when that one suitor calls. Still, that one suitor will need to be willing to accept the risk that, if Rodgers doesn’t have things go the way he wants, he’ll choose to do again the same thing he did this week.

#2743. Eagles News: “One of the darkest Thanksgiving Day games ever for the Dallas Cowboys”

Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles news and links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

Man. What a great game. What an awesome Thanksgiving. This 2026 season has largely stunk. But that win is a moment in time we'll always have forever. And one that'll haunt the Cowboys and their fans. Thank you, Joe Milton, DeVonta Smith, Ty Robinson, Jake Elliott, and … the whole team. GBDH.

Let's get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

Cowboys vs. Eagles recap: Dallas embarrassed by Philadelphia on Thanksgiving Day – Blogging The Boys

It will go down in history as one of the darkest Thanksgiving Day games ever for the Dallas Cowboys. Somehow, some way, the Cowboys threw away a 31-10 lead that they had in the third quarter. The Philadelphia Eagles won on what was basically a game-winning, 60-yard field goal. It is hard to fathom. On the other hand it is actually very easy to fathom given everything we have seen from the Cowboys this season. They are not a good football team. They are poorly coached. They are talent-deficient. They are all of the bad things. On a day where we are supposed to be thankful it is hard to find a reason to be for this specific part of our lives. The Dallas Cowboys are a weekly embarrassment and Thursday was the latest example of it. What even happens now?

10 Eagles things I think I think after incredible comeback vs. Cowboys – BGN

Incredible. There's no other way to describe the Philadelphia Eagles' comeback victory over the Dallas Cowboys — which was way more enjoyable than any meal you could consume on Thanksgiving. This is an Eagles game that's going to be remembered forever, just like the Christmas Day win over the Cowboys in 2006 and the Miracle at the Meadowlands comeback in 2010. The victory is that improbable, especially when the Eagles were down 31-10 with 3:35 left in the third quarter. They had no business being in this game, yet they found their way back to make it a game — and stole a victory away from the Cowboys on Thanksgiving. This was a game the Cowboys should have won handily. Instead they choked it away, thanks to the hands of a resilient Eagles team that didn't let their 3-7 record stand in the way of what seemed to be an insurmountable deficit. No matter how the rest of this season goes, that was one heck of a win. This victory will be talked about amongst generations of Eagles fans. A Thanksgiving miracle — that may have ended the Cowboys season. The Eagles are good at ruining seasons all of a sudden.

NFL Thanksgiving Winners & Losers – SB Nation

Winner: Joe Milton. I don't know what the long-term future is for the Eagles at quarterback, but Milton's performance on Thanksgiving is going to lead to some uncomfortable conversations. I don't think he's a perfect quarterback by any stretch of the imagination, but he's certainly close enough to Jalen Hurts that it's increasingly difficult to justify paying a QB $51M AAV, when there's someone playing equally well you could pay much, much less. Milton played solid football and didn't let the moment get too big for him. This is also a guy who is on a one year, $1 million contract — and now there are going to be teams putting him on their free agent list. There's a lot of football to go, but that was a statement game.

Eagles-Cowboys: MR. ROCKET Joe Milton With Eagles Thanksgiving MIRACLE Win, Brandon Graham Reacts – PHLY Sports

Joe Milton delivered one of the more memorable games by an Eagles QB in recent memory with two long bombs to DeVonta Smith, a rushing touchdown and a last-second drive following the biggest defensive stand of the game which set up an unreal 60-yard Jake Elliott game-winner. The shocking win gave the Eagles a shocking win to bring them to 4-7 and keep their slim playoff hopes alive. Brandon Graham joins Brandon Lee Gowton, Bo Wulf, Miles Johnson, Fran Duffy and EJ Smith to break it all down.

'It was just chaos:' Inside the Eagles locker room after improbable Thanksgiving comeback vs. Cowboys – PHLY Eagles

"There's no better day, Thanksgiving game against the Cowboys, against a division rival, against a great quarterback like Dak," Robinson said of notching his first career sack. "The adversity we overcame with the guys on the defensive side of the ball, there's no better feeling — I haven't had kids yet, so I don't know what that's like, but as of right know, that's probably No. 1 for me." Perhaps the most improbable contributor was Milton. The 26-year-old who started the season on the Cowboys practice squad going against Dallas defense as a scout-teamer supercharged the Eagles offense, one unbelievably rifled throw at a time. Milton went 21-for-31 for 311 yards and three passing touchdowns and achieved the rare feat of doing something on a football field that even a collection of professional football players couldn't believe was possible. He threw a ball 64.4 yards through the air, crossing from one sideline to the other and into the sure hands of DeVonta Smith for a 50-yard touchdown. "I don't know how far that first ball went to Smitty," Ertz said. "But it had to be one of the farthest throws I've ever seen. … It's insane. Rolling away, Smitty's going right, he's going left. Just a really impressive throw."

Thanksgiving NFL football had it all: Comebacks, walk-offs and plenty of points – ESPN

Of Milton's 311 passing yards, 276 (88.7%) came through air yards; only 35 came after the catch. Since 1992 — as far back as ESPN Research can take us — this is the only game of at least 300 passing yards with 40 or fewer yards after the catch. That should not be a surprise, because this is not how football has ever worked on the material plane. Milton threw so far downfield and so fearlessly into the sideline that receivers were either basically out of bounds or already in the end zone upon the ball's arrival. The middle of the field, where the entire modern game is played, is for mortal men. What is a checkdown to someone with this kind of arm? On the other side, these 2026 Cowboys are a particularly compelling team to watch lose given the spectacular scale of their collapses. The 5-7 Cowboys had a 99.4% win probability at the peak of this game, per ESPN's model. They let a listless Eagles team that had not scored more than 22 points in a game since Week 2 score 22 points in the fourth quarter alone. This was the second home game the Cowboys have lost this season in which they led by at least 14 points in the fourth quarter (the other being the Week 8 loss to Arizona). According to the Elias Sport Bureau, they are the only team to achieve that feat in a season in NFL history.

Handing out 10 awards from the Eagles-Cowboys Thanksgiving game – PhillyVoice

1) The 'Warrior' Award 🪖: DeVonta Smith. DeVonta Smith was a star in this game, catching 11 passes on 14 targets for 200 yards and 2 TDs. Postgame, Smith could barely walk, and even when he was able to make it to his locker stall, he could barely move. A team employee had to help him take his socks off. Given what he looked like after the game, it's remarkable that Smith was able to finish it. He was a warrior.

The Miracle At The Metroplex – Iggles Blitz

While it was to see the Eagles offense score 32 points, we do need to remember that they did it against the worst defense in the NFC. I'd love to tell you Milton will play like that again, but that could have been lightning in a bottle. We need to see him play several more games to have a real feel for who he is. Milton showed today that his special physical traits do translate to the field. He's not just made for the Scouting Combine. The Eagles may have found a young QB worth developing.

Thanksgiving tripleheader: What We Learned from Bears-Lions, Eagles-Cowboys, Chiefs-Bills – NFL.com

Bazooka Joe Milton III leads stunning Eagles comeback vs. Cowboys. The Eagles looked dead in the water, missing starters all over the field, playing with a backup QB, and were down 31-10 deep in the third quarter. Then the largest comeback in Thanksgiving history began with Joe Milton's big arm. The QB splashed fearless bombs over and over again to puncture a limp Cowboys defense. With Saquon Barkley out early with an injury, Milton diced up the Dallas defense, completing 21 of 31 passes for 331 yards, three TDs and an INT. Several of his heaves to DeVonta Smith (11 catches, 200 receiving yards, two TDs) were perfectly dropped in the bucket. Milton might not yet have consistent touch underneath or on intermediate throws, vacillating from laser to a ball four feet off the mark (see: fourth quarter INT). However, he throws a beautiful deep ball, particularly on the move. Case in point: 188 yards and all three TDs came on passes of 20-plus air yards (56.8%). Milton's rushing ability also provides pizzazz to an offense that couldn't get off the ground until Week 12. The Eagles switched to Bazooka Joe to inject explosives into a bland turkey of an offense. Boy, did that come to fruition on Thursday. He brings a cannon arm and athletic ability to overcome blocking deficiencies. He still has strides to make, and he will have to do it against a defense better than Dallas' to prove he can be a legit starter in 2027. But he jolted a sleepy game and turned it on its head. Milton makes the four-win Eagles immensely more watchable the rest of the way.

How Eagles QB Joe Milton rocketed into 'rock star' status on Thanksgiving vs. Cowboys – The Athletic

Perhaps the next start is better than this one, and the Eagles improbably turn around the season like they improbably turned this game around. In the locker room, they're not thinking that yet. Milton said he lived in the moment Thursday. The team is doing the same. But one can't help but wonder what this night means for his career. He's a restricted free agent at season's end. The Eagles weren't the only ones who saw it. The rest of the league is watching. It was one of the NFL's great quarterbacks on the broadcast. "The guy's a rock star, man," Mailata said. "Hats off to him, man. MVP." Milton was minutes past speaking with Brady — who said he was speechless — when Mailata made that comment. The hype was for Milton. He was the star on Thanksgiving.

Jake Elliott proves again he's one of the great long-distance kickers in history – NBCSP

However you measure it, Elliott reaffirmed his status Thursday as one of the greatest long-distance kickers in NFL history and one of the greatest clutch kickers ever. "I mean, yeah, I'm human," Elliott said after the game. "Definitely nervous, but you you just go back to your process. I mean, everything, every (kick) is the same. I treat it the same and just kind of have my process: What balls I'm hitting to the nets, at what times, and when I feel comfortable about about the timing of everything, everything usually goes well." It has lately. Elliott has now made three field goals of at least 55 yards in three attempts this year and his four career makes from 59 yards and out are tied for 4th-most in NFL history. This is a guy who was statistically the worst kicker in the NFL over the 2024 and 2025 seasons. Elliott is now 4-for-5 in his career from 59 yards, tied with Little for most accurate ever from that distance. Elliott thought he had a game-winning 48-yarder with eight seconds left against the Jaguars in London, only to watch Little turn the tables and make a 57-yarder as time expired. He finally got to experience a game-winner for the first time since October 2023, when he made a 54-yarder in overtime to beat the Commanders 34-31 at th Linc. "It's awesome," Elliott said. "We haven't had one for a little bit. We almost had one in London, but it's always good to be in those situations." It speaks volumes that for all the big throws Joe Milton made Thursday night he said his favorites were the two short passes that got the Eagles into position for a long-distane game winner.

Ty Robinson: From 'life support' to Eagles hero on Thanksgiving – PhiladelphiaEagles.com

In a game full of heroes for the Eagles, the comeback against the Cowboys would not have been possible without Ty Robinson. Not only did he sack Dak Prescott on fourth down to set up Jake Elliott's game-winning field goal, the second-year defensive tackle's punt block at the start of the fourth quarter couldn't have come at a better time. Down 31-10, quarterback Joe Milton was able to connect with wide receiver DeVonta Smith deep downfield for a 45-yard touchdown to make it a two-possession game. The Eagles' defense then made a quick stop in Cowboy's territory, forcing Cowboys to punt. Robinson and Chance Campbell lined up to the right side of the Cowboys' punt formation, with Michael Carter II and Kenny Moore II set to rush off opposite ends. At the snap, Campbell looped around Robinson's right on a stunt, freeing Robinson to shed a block while going left. "That was one of the rushes we had planned going into the short week," Robinson said of the punt rush. "Me and Chance (Campbell) were just pumping each other up out there, talking about, 'Let's go get one.' When I went to go pick the (blocker), he wrapped and the guard came off. I just felt a lot of open space. I just stuck my hand out and tried to get out of the way, so I didn't hit the punter. I didn't even see it hit my hand. I just felt it."

Like it or not, Nick Sirianni will sink or swim — like in thriller over Cowboys — doing it his way – Inquirer

The coach certainly is not without his flaws, as anyone who watched his postgame antics can attest — including judge, jury, and executioner Jeffrey Lurie. But the Eagles owner may look past a seven-game losing streak, an often-inefficient offense, and overall sloppy football and see this season's regression as a byproduct of misfortune more than incompetence. Certainly there is a case to be made that losing your starting quarterback, Hall of Fame-bound right tackle, and multiple skill-position players would be insurmountable for most. And yet, Sirianni's Eagles have kept one arm in front of the other through it all. "It's about fighting through adversity, a lot of adversity, throughout this season," Sirianni said of his Chadwick messaging. "The whole message is sometimes you can find yourself in situations that you weren't anticipating, and in those situations, can you keep swimming? "You never know how close you are to getting out of the situation. But you got to keep fighting through it all." With upcoming games against the lowly Cardinals and Colts, it isn't outlandish to believe that the 4-7 Eagles could get back to .500. But catching the 6-3-1 Giants probably is out of their grasp. A few more wins may only deprive them of higher draft position. Sirianni has built anything but a culture of losing. He's won as often as any coach over the last six years. While most of the credit he receives from outside the Eagles focuses on what he does off the field, he's not the bumbling caricature some have created when it comes to scheme.

Nick Sirianni is pulled away from fans after comeback win – PFT

Good or bad, right or wrong, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni has had from time to time the demeanor of a fan who won a contest to be the head coach for a day. On Thursday in Dallas, he displayed those qualities after a stunning come-from-way-behind win over the Cowboys. While celebrating the 39-38 win (they trailed 31-10, late in the third quarter), Sirianni approached fans in field-level suites. He eventually had to be pulled away by Dom DiSandro.

We Must Always Remain Thankful For The Dallas Cowboys – Defector

All the Cowboys had to do in order to avoid suffering a historic Thanksgiving collapse was protect a 21-point second-half lead. All they had to do was not get a punt blocked for a touchdown. All they had to do was make a 40-yard field goal that would have put them up 11 with 3:27 left to play. All they had to do was not get sacked on a fourth-and-1 attempt with 55 seconds left. All they had to do was not commit a pass interference penalty on third down with 23 seconds left to play. All they had to do was not be the Cowboys for once. Thank god they can't do that.

NFC playoff picture: NFC East looks like two-horse race with Giants and Commanders – Big Blue View

The Dallas Cowboys' stunning meltdown on Thursday night against the Philadelphia Eagles, blowing at 31-10 late-third quarter lead in a 39-38 defeat, changed the NFC East title race. The Washington Commanders are now the only team that appears to have a realistic chance of catching the first place New York Giants. As of Friday morning, NFL.com gives the Giants a 70% chance of making the playoffs. That rises to 78% if rthey defeat the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. It falls to 53% should they lose. The Commanders currently sit with a 24% chance to make the playoffs. The Cowboys? NFL.com says Dallas (5-7) now has just an 8% chance of making the playoffs.

Commanders vs. Cardinals Thursday injury report: Treylon Burks limited – Hogs Haven

Treylon Burks has been bothered with a foot injury for several weeks. The veteran Commanders receiver initially suffered the injury weeks ago and Washington has been trying their best to manage it while keeping him in the lineup. He missed the Rams game but has found a way to play in every other game, and the strategy of limiting his practice work has been effective in getting him ready for game day. It's clearly limiting his production, but his presence is key to keeping this offense moving.

Commanders sign another former 49ers' draft pick to practice squad – CommandersWire

A key reserve for San Francisco's secondary, Ambry Thomas fractured his forearm during the 2024 preseason and was placed on injured reserve. The 49ers released him in December. The Indianapolis Colts quickly claimed him off waivers, but he failed his physical and was released the next day. Then, the Minnesota Vikings signed Thomas to their practice squad. He spent the offseason with the Vikings, but was released as part of their final roster cuts in 2025. He then signed with the Philadelphia Eagles and spent the entire season on their practice squad and was released in August.

#2742. Celtics will be without key player against Hawks

BOSTON — The Celtics will be without Mitchell Robinson when they host the Atlanta Hawks on Friday night in their final NBA Cup Group Play game. Robinson, initially listed as questionable, has been downgraded to out due to an illness.

Robinson has been sidelined due to illness for four straight games: he missed the Celtics' games the Sacramento Kings, Golden State Warriors, Washington Wizards, and now the Atlanta Hawks. Unrelatedly, he also sat out the Celtics' November 1st game in Orlando for rest.

Robinson has appeared in 14 games, including five starts, and is averaging 5.4 rebounds per game, the fewest of his career. He also has the team's worst on-off rating.

But Brad Stevens said last week that he expects Robinson to figure it out.

"You can tell it's obviously a transition for him, and that's not all that atypical for guys, and so again, it's so early that we'll see how this all plays out," Stevens said. "But I trust that what he does when he's at his best will translate because it always has, right?"

With Robinson out, Neemias Queta will continue to anchor the Celtics' frontcourt, while Luka Garza and rookie Chris Cenac Jr. could see increased minutes behind him. Queta averages 10.4 points, 6.9 rebounds, 2.0 assists, and 1.2 blocks in 23.4 minutes per game; on Tuesday, he scored 21 points on 9-for-11 shooting.

"Obviously, as the years go by, I think I'm also [entering] my prime, so I'm becoming more confident, more comfortable out there," Queta said at Celtics shootaround on Friday morning.

The Celtics snapped a four-game losing streak with a 131-116 win over the Washington Wizards on Tuesday night, behind 41 points from Jayson Tatum and 28 from Paul George.

#2741. Nvidia's billion-dollar board bet: Who's protected as lawsuits mount?

Jensen Huang is back as CEO of Nvidia, after President Donald Trump urged the company's board to rehire Huang. But investigations into the company, its executive leadership and its board continue as outside criticism mounts.

"Clearly they caved to external pressure," said Betsy Atkins, an author and longtime public-company director. "The board failed," she said, when it initially allowed Huang's removal. "The board's role is to think of all stakeholders."

California Attorney General Rob Bonta is investigating whether Nvidia misrepresented information to investors. "There is classic corporate securities law on the books in California that prevents investors and the public from being misled by companies," Bonta said on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Tuesday.

Directors are already defendants in a shareholder lawsuit accusing them of failing to oversee Nvidia. A separate securities class action targets the company and Huang, its co-founder.

Now the board’s insurance choices are part of the story. A risk advisor with direct knowledge of Nvidia’s coverage, who asked not to be named because they are not authorized to speak publicly about client matters, said the company built an approximately $1 billion D&O tower, insurance jargon for directors and officers insurance policies from different companies that combine to cover one massive risk.

Nvidia "loves insurance," the advisor said. “They buy insurance as if they have no balance sheet.”

A billion-dollar tower would essentially mean Nvidia "bought the market," purchasing all the coverage it could get, according to another industry expert, who has 25 years working in financial insurance. The expert asked not to be named due to sensitivity surrounding relationships with past or potential future clients.

But Nvidia directed all that coverage to Side A only, according to the risk advisor. Side A protects directors and officers personally when the company cannot indemnify them. Side B covers the company for legal defense costs or settlements on behalf of directors and officers, and Side C protects the company when it's named as a defendant in a suit such as a securities claim.

The risk advisor says Nvidia believed it had "the war chest" to protect itself against a securities class action suit.

That choice is raising questions about whether the board protected itself at the company’s expense. CNBC asked Nvidia for comment but received no response.

An insurance CEO, who asked not to be named in order to protect client relationships, characterized a billion-dollar policy as a lot of coverage, but said a Side A-only allocation was a surprising move because it results in imbalanced coverage, protecting only directors.

That structure is not automatically a governance failure, according to the D&O insurance expert with long experience in coverage for banks, drugmakers and other businesses that often face litigation. Side A-only programs are common among companies with the capital to manage the corporate risk internally.

"For a company with Nvidia’s resources, retaining the company-side risk can make financial sense," said the industry expert with 25 years working in financial insurance. It's Side A D&O that's "imperative to corporate governance."

"It is a capital-allocation decision," the expert said. The company decides that buying insurance for its own balance sheet is not worth the premium. In other words, Side B and Side C are considered too expensive for the coverage the company gets.

The question for shareholders is whether the board’s decision to hold that risk was a sound use of the company’s resources and whether the company can absorb the costs if the claims grow.

A shareholder derivative complaint filed Nov. 11 names Huang, directors and other officers. It alleges that they failed to oversee risks involving Huang’s relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang and made misleading statements. It also alleges that some defendants sold roughly $2 billion in Nvidia stock while holding material nonpublic information. Those remain allegations, not findings.

A separate securities class action, filed Nov. 9, names Nvidia and Huang. It seeks damages for investors who bought Nvidia shares between Oct. 9, 2025, and Nov. 8, 2026, alleging the company and Huang misled investors.

The distinction matters: The derivative suit is brought on Nvidia’s behalf, while the class action seeks recovery for investors.

"Insurance is already at work," said Michel Léonard, chief economist at the Insurance Information Institute, describing standard policy mechanics, not Nvidia’s specific policy. "Once the suit is filed, D&O starts paying defense costs, long before anyone proves anything."

A claim still has to meet the policy’s terms, and defense costs can reduce the remaining limits. Nor does a drop in Nvidia’s market value by itself establish an insurable loss. Plaintiffs would need to prove legally recoverable damages; the policy would respond only to covered losses.

The board has already taken steps it says are aimed at accountability. Nvidia announced an independent investigation on Nov. 8, and independent directors retained outside counsel two days later. Huang resigned as CEO and a director on Nov. 11; the board appointed CFO Colette Kress interim CEO. Nvidia said it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets had been compromised by Huang's extramarital relationships.

Atkins, who joined the board of Wynn Resorts in 2018 after founder Steve Wynn resigned, said allegations are not conclusions and that boards should also weigh governance concerns against the value a founder brings to a company’s innovation. Nvidia's investigation is continuing even as Huang resumes leadership.

“Will companies’ hyper-accelerated innovation speed be the same without them? I don’t think so,” said Atkins, author of "Don't Waste a Board Seat: A Decision-Maker's Guide to Choosing Directors Who Create Value."

Nvidia’s 2026 proxy also says the company has indemnity agreements with its directors and officers — separate from its insurance. Those agreements provide for the company to cover certain costs and liabilities when the law permits.

#2740. Brian Schottenheimer on failed fourth-down try: "I trust our quarterback and our offense"

The Eagles’ path to erasing a 31-10 third-quarter deficit included many favorable twists and turns. The last one was a gift from the Cowboys.

With 55 seconds left — and with the Eagles having no timeouts — the Cowboys faced fourth and one from the Philadelphia 39. After attempting to get the Eagles to jump offside, the Cowboys took a timeout and decided to go for it.

The Cowboys lined up in shotgun formation. Quarterback Dak Prescott looked to the right, presumably to connect on a slant to receiver CeeDee Lamb. Lamb was jammed hard by cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. Prescott waited for Lamb to get free. When Prescott decided to pursue another option, he was sacked.

The play lost nine yards, giving the Eagles the ball at their own 48.

Why not punt? Why not force quarterback Joe Milton III to drive into field-goal range, with less than 50 seconds to play and no timeouts?

Coach Brian Schottenheimer was asked about the decision after the game.

“Really felt good about the drive we had going, and felt really good that we were gonna put the game away there,” Schottenheimer told reporters. “And I wanted the ball in Dak’s hands. And, unfortunately, we weren’t able to make it work.”

Does Schottenheimer ever second-guess himself?

“All the time,” he said. “Not in that situation. Absolutely not in that situation.”

“I trust our quarterback and our offense,” Schottenheimer said.

That’s fine. But it’s not about “trust.” It’s about whether it makes sense to assume the offense will execute in that moment, and what the consequence will be if the defense executes a little better.

It’s about making an assessment, based on years of watching, playing, and coaching football, as to whether the risk of not converting outweighed the risk of the Eagles driving from their own 20 (or perhaps deep inside their own 20) into field goal range.

Maybe the truth is that Schottenheimer didn’t trust his defense to keep that from happening. Regardless, his “trust” in the offense was ultimately misplaced. And the Cowboys lost another game when they scored 30 or more points.

#2737. Luka Doncic told Lakers front office to get Walker Kessler this offseason

Walker Kessler has been everything the Lakers needed him to be this season: 14 points a game on 66.9% shooting, plus 10.8 rebounds and 2.1 blocks per night (third in the league). He's been setting picks and rolling hard to the rim on offense, and on defense he's been the backstop in the paint the Lakers needed to allow their wing defenders to be disruptive and force turnovers.

Luka Doncic said he told Lakers GM Rob Pelinka this offseason to get Kessler, in an interview with ESPN's Dave McMenamin.

"I told them after the season I wanted Walker," Doncic told ESPN of an offseason conversation he had with Rob Pelinka, Lakers president of basketball operations and general manager, and the front office.

"I think he's a really good player," Doncic continued. "Obviously, last season he didn't play. He played like five games. Obviously [Utah] kept him out, but just playing against him in the previous years, it was hard to score. He was protecting the rim, he was dominating the paint. So just after the season, I went to them and said, 'I want Walker.'"

The price to get Kessler out of Utah was steep: two first-round picks (2031 and 2033) and two pick swaps (2028 and 2030), but it's one the Lakers had to pay to best reshape the roster around Doncic. The biggest risk from the Lakers' perspective was health, Kessler played just five games the previous season due to shoulder surgery and had not played in 65 or more games since his rookie season.

It has worked. The Lakers have the best record in the West and sit atop the conference heading into a showdown with San Antonio on Friday night. Both the Lakers' offense and defense are more than six points per 100 possessions better when Kessler is on the court, and the team's biggest challenge right now is non-Kessler minutes (look for them to be active heading toward the trade deadline).

This has all worked out just as Doncic has envisioned.

#2736. Raiders surprising move bestows major respect on Fernando Mendoza

Two starts into his NFL career, Fernando Mendoza has earned the distinction of being named a Raiders captain.

And he's in some pretty elite company, joining Maxx Crosby as one of three captains for Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns. Special teams ace Dylan Laube is the third.

Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza celebrates a touchdown pass against the Denver Broncos in Denver, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/David Zalubowski

The Raiders select their captains on a weekly basis, based on a set of criteria established by first-year coach Klint Kubiak. Among the attributes Kubiak emphasizes are work ethic, performance, diligence and how players conduct themselves throughout the practice week.

That Mendoza has already checked enough of those boxes to earn the designation speaks volumes about how he's handled himself since taking over as the Raiders' starting quarterback.

Mendoza will make just his third career start Sunday night in Cleveland, where he'll look to build on the significant progress he made last week against the Broncos.

The first overall pick in April's draft completed 18 of 37 passes for 267 yards and three touchdowns while adding 22 yards rushing against one of the NFL's most formidable defenses.

Among his highlights were a 68-yard touchdown pass to Ashton Jeanty, a 19-yard scoring strike to tight end Ian Thomas and a seven-yard touchdown pass to Jack Bech.

Maxx Crosby of the Las Vegas Raiders reacts during a game against the Seattle Seahawks in Las Vegas on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images

Perhaps most impressive was how Mendoza kept his composure after the Raiders fell behind 17-0, engineering three consecutive scoring drives to pull them even in the third quarter.

There were some growing pains, including five sacks and a late interception that was returned for a touchdown. But the improvement from his starting debut against the Seahawks was unmistakable.

Now comes another significant challenge against a talented Browns defense in his first NFL prime-time start.

Dylan Laube (23) of the Las Vegas Raiders celebrates a tackle against the New York Jets in East Rutherford, New Jersey, Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Getty Images

The captaincy is noteworthy because, under Kubiak, it isn't automatically bestowed upon the starting quarterback. It's something that has to be earned, irrespective of salary, draft status or position.

The Raiders have entrusted Mendoza with the future of their franchise. He's already demonstrating an understanding of the responsibilities that come with it.

#2734. Semiconductor chips are the new oil. Here's why

The artificial intelligence boom has pushed semiconductors past oil and gas in global export value for the first time, according to a Deutsche Bank analysis of International Trade Centre data.

Yet the milestone arrives at an awkward moment, just as investors reassess the outlook for artificial intelligence spending and drive down the price of semiconductor stocks. Last week, before Monday's breathtaking reversal, semiconductor stocks suffered their worst weekly loss in a quarter century, with the PHLX Semiconductor Index (SOX) plunging nearly 11% last Friday alone, capping a more than 17% weekly decline.

Nvidia soared more than 31% Monday after the leading maker of artificial intelligence chips had fallen for a seventh straight week, plunging 46% during that stretch. Then it fell again, dropping almost 10% on Tuesday and Wednesday. Advanced Micro Devices tumbled 20% in two days last Thursday and Friday. Micron Technology sank 27% over the seven days ended last Friday.

"For decades we've talked about the petrodollar. Perhaps increasingly we need to think about the chip dollar," Jim Reid, global head of macro and thematic research at Deutsche Bank wrote in a report this month.

Semiconductor exports overtook oil and gas for the first time during the January-March quarter of 2026, reaching about $1.61 trillion, compared with $1.53 trillion for oil and gas, the report said, using four-quarter rolling totals.

The gap widened in the second quarter, when semiconductor exports totaled about $1.60 trillion and oil and gas exports reached about $1.47 trillion. Disruptions to oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz after the Iran war helped widen the gap. Daily oil flows through the Strait collapsed nearly 77%, to 4.9 million barrels in the second quarter of 2026 from 21.6 million barrels in the fourth quarter of 2025, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

Yet the demand for semiconductors has proven insatiable in the face of soaring data center construction, boosting global trade in the increasingly scarce AI component. Hundreds of billions of dollars of orders for graphics processing units and data centers aim at providing AI computing power, Rothschild & Co. Redburn wrote in a report last Thursday.

"Compute will be the new commodity fueling this transformation on a global scale," Rothschild analyst Cara Thomson said.

The shift toward chips has macroeconomic implications just as the explosion in oil trade did in the 1970s.

Oil-exporting countries historically recycled much of their surpluses into the purchase of U.S. Treasuries and other bonds, helping finance U.S. deficits and underpin demand for other government debt.

Reid at Deutsche Bank said that since semiconductor-surplus countries in Asia are more closely tied to U.S. tech companies, some chip-export earnings could flow back into U.S. technology stocks, startups and data centers, further helping to finance the AI investment cycle.

The changing dynamics in global trade could also tilt the mix of global financial flows, Reid said. "So welcome to the chip-dollar era: potentially more growth, more excitement, more volatility, and structurally higher yields" in corporate and government debt.

#2732. Chargers-Patriots Game Preview: How will Mike McDaniel warp the offense for D.J. Uiagalelei?

The Chargers (1-9) are back at home this week to face the Patriots (5-5) in the hopes of earning their first win inside SoFi Stadium this season. New England is coming off their bye week and have had two weeks to get backup quarterback Tommy DeVito up to speed in the wake of Drake Maye's injury that will sideline him until at least the postseason.

Two inexperienced backup quarterbacks are not what most fans would like to watch during a football game in Novemeber, but sometimes that's the reality of the NFL. To look at this from a more positive view, fans of both teams will get their first look at their backups to see what their team truly has behind the starters. This could be a good or bad experience, but overall everyone will leave the day more enlightened! That's a win, right?

The Chargers are playing for nothing but their own prides while the Patriots are still fighting to right the ship and hopefully find a way into the postseason. Both teams have dealt with injuries this year to impact players, and that goes beyond the quarterback spot. Wideout A.J. Brown will not play in this one which is a good thing for a Chargers defense that could be without half of their starting unit on Sunday.

Being short-handed like that never fun, and it makes the hopes that DJU could somehow lead them to an improbable victory even slimmer.

But hey, when everyone is going poorly, all you can do is throw your hands up and try to enjoy the ride.

Below are the three things I'll be watching closely when these teams take the field on Sunday.

Just like everyone would have predicted before the season began, the quarterback matchup for the Chargers' rematch with the Patriots is D.J. Uiagalelei and Tommy DeVito. Better grab your popcorn!

Uiagalelei is a second-year UDFA who only has one seven career pass attempts to his name, all of which came in garbage time against the Texans. He completed only two passes in those snaps, but one did go for a touchdown to Derius Davis.

DeVito comes into this game with eight starts under his belt and nine career touchdown passes to four inteceptions. He has not started a game this year, but has thrown for 132 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in three appearances.

With two inexperienced quarterbacks on the field, you can fully expected both defenses to rev up their pass rush early and often to rattle them as soon as possible.

It's not like the Chargers were throwing the ball all that much before Justin Herbert's concussion, but it's likely to be even less without the Chargers starting quarterback.

The Chargers have run the football at least 30 times in each of their last three games. They rushed for 138 yards against the Texans, 160 against the Ravens, and 158 against the Texans. Omarion Hampton scored against the Ravens but Herbert has the other two rushing touchdowns over those three games with one coming against the Ravens and Jets, apiece.

Uiagalelei also has the athleticism to produce on the ground if he wants, and it'll be interesting to see if McDaniel uses him in a similar way as Herbert as of late.

In all honesty, I would not be shocked if the Chargers set a new season-high for rushing attempts in a game against the Patriots. It would minimize the pressure on DJU and keep the play-action game alive to make sure the defense can't get to overeager against such a green player.

If all goes well, maybe we get Hampton's second 100-yard game of the season, as well.

The Chargers defense looked the worst they have all year against the Jets in a game where starting linebacker Daiyan Henley and cornerback Tarheeb Still were sidelined with injuries. Star safety Derwin James has also missed the past month and isn't coming back for multiple weeks while on IR.

As of Friday morning, the Chargers were on pace to play a number of backups on defense thanks to a laundry list of a injury report through the first two practices.

Henley and Still have not practiced in any capacity and will likely miss another week. Joining them on the sidelines through Wednesday and Thursday were edge rushers Tuli Tuipulotu and Akheem Mesidor, and defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson. If all of those latter three do not practice in some way on Friday, the Chargers could play the Patriots without half of their starting defense.

The secondary is already a shallow group and now the front seven gets even thinner if two of the team's top three edge rushers are forced to miss Sunday. It would be Bud Dupree starting opposite Khalil Mack and Caleb Murphy as the No. 3 pass rusher.

Once again, the linebacker rotation will feature Del'Shawn Phillips, Marlowe Wax, Troy Dye, and veteran Denzel Perryman. No studs by any means and they'll have to do better at stopping the run game which New England will likely try to lean on, especially seeing how consistent the Jets were at getting chunks in Week 11.

Looking at this injury report, the Chargers will have to get a number of depth pieces to play above themselves in over to avoid falling to 1-10.
