#2731. Average Four Factor Index Power Rankings: 2026-2027 NBA Season Week 6

In contrast to the week prior, this last week has seen remarkable stability in the aFFI power rankings, with no team moving more than three spots in any direction. However, this lack of dynamism doesn't mean that we haven't gained valuable information, as I'll detail below. Furthermore, I am introducing a new deep-dive section on the Spurs aFFI performance, so please let me know what you think!

We'll get to the broader rankings (and San Antonio's position within them) shortly, but before that I'd like to provide a little aFFI deep-dive to illustrate how the Silver and Black have been performing in individual games, and how those performances have driven its season-long aFFI-value.

The quickest way to summarize the last week is that San Antonio's overall aFFI (i.e., it's "season aFFI") is little changed, having ticked down slightly from 59.43 to 59.13. The three games they have played since last Friday include two impressive wins against admittedly weak competition, as well as a frustrating loss against Portland in which a brilliant performance by Wemby was undermined by weak play across the rest of the team.

Digging into the "game aFFI" values for each of these contests (which capture the Spurs' four factor performance relative to their opponent in each individual game), we see that these contests were decided in very different ways. For example, San Antonio's win over New Orleans was driven entirely by an exceptional effective field goal percentage differential of +14.5 percentage points, which corresponds to a ∆EFG% percentile value of 94.32 (i.e., 94.32% of all other regular season effective field goal percentage differentials achieved by NBA teams since the 2012-2013 season have been worse). In contrast, the Spurs ∆EFG% percentile in the Sacramento game was just 42.68, but they were excellent with respect to every other factor, especially their FTM/FTA differential. San Antonio's effective field goal percentage differential was also slightly below-median in the Blazers loss, but a dismal ∆TOV% percentile (13.6) pushed their game aFFI down significantly.

Looking at the league as a whole, we see that not much has changed since last week, especially at the top. In fact, six of the top ten teams (including San Antonio) have the same ranking as before, and the four remaining teams have moved up or down by just one spot. Furthermore, the top four teams remain exceptionally close according to their season-long aFFI, with just 1.2 points separating first-ranked Minnesota (60.33) from the fourth-ranked Spurs (59.13). These four teams have been extremely close for most of the young season, and it will be interesting to see if any one of them begins to stand above the rest in the weeks ahead.

Across the entire league, the Miami Heat have achieved the largest rise in aFFI ranking, moving up three spots since last week and getting within a half-point of the top ten. Several teams have moved up two spots, with Dallas being the highest-ranking member of that set at #13.

On the opposite end of the spectrum, Cleveland and OKC have both dropped three positions since last Friday and appear poised to fall further, though from a practical point of view these two team's have divergent outlooks. Specifically, Cleveland could likely continue its poor play and remain in the playoff picture, whereas the injury-plagued Thunder have already fallen out of the play-in set in the West. Even though OKC is expected to get some of its key players back before the end of the season, those reinforcements may simply arrive too late to make any difference.

Although the overall aFFI rankings have remained pretty static this week, Figure 3 reveals that a more detailed set of tiers may be emerging:

Clear Contenders (5 teams) — Not much has changed at the top, except to say that last week's "emerging contenders list" appears to be splitting in two, with five teams (Minnesota, Memphis, Houston, San Antonio, and the Lakers) setting themselves apart at the very top. Movement within the top four teams has been fluid, with teams moving up and down one or two spots depending on the outcome of individual games. Los Angeles sits slightly farther back but may rise or fall dramatically as their schedule gets significantly tougher in the days ahead (starting tonight against the Spurs).

Potential Contenders (4 teams) — Outside of the top five, aFFI values begin spreading out, with a gap of about 3.4 points separating sixth-ranked Boston (57.8) from ninth-ranked New York (54.41). All four of the teams within this range have shown flashes of brilliance and an ability to beat the best (see Portland's victory over San Antonio on Wednesday); however, they have also lacked consistency and each have six losses.

Likely Playoff/Play-in Participants (8 teams) — Within this eclectic group, Philadelphia and Atlanta continue to stand out as having exceptional records relative to their aFFI ranking. This is particularly true of the 76ers, who sit firmly atop the East despite having a middling point differential of +2.2 and an aFFI value of just 51.69. Similarly, the Hawks' aFFI score suggests that they should be a slightly below 0.500 team, yet they are currently 11-6 and seeded fourth in the East. It is still very early in the season, but the true nature of both teams may be revealed soon, as they have difficult schedules over the next week.

Fading Hope (6 teams) — Some of these teams are probably not too surprised to fall into this category; in particular, having marginal playoff hopes but no real chance at success seems to be the default setting in Chicago and Orlando. Fans of the remaining teams in this set probably have more complex emotions. For example, Washington fans are likely torn between joy over not being terrible for the first time in years and the haunting realization that their offseason additions are overpaid and underwhelming. Indiana and Toronto fans are doubtless disappointed thus far, though the Raptors can at least take solace in the fact that Kawhi Leonard's injury has played a large role in their lackluster season to date (shocker). Finally, the Suns are likely feeling pretty good about their chances to move up, as they have played quite well after starting the season terribly.

Was There Ever Really a Chance? (5 teams) — Every member of this group (Brooklyn, the Clippers, Utah, New Orleans, and Charlotte) is effectively eliminated from the playoff picture barring any shocking developments, but I suspect their respective fan bases feel quite differently about that position. For example, it is hard to imagine anyone thinking that New Orleans, Brooklyn, or the Clippers had a realistic chance of success heading into this season. However, there was some buzz surrounding Utah's potential, and quite a few people thought that the Hornets' offseason moves were going to vault them firmly into the East's playoff picture. They may still get there, but only with a dramatic turn of the tide.

Kings' Corner (2 teams) — On the bright side, both the Kings and Bucks have doubled their season win total in the last week, which allows both fanbases to use the plural "wins" for the first time all season. Unfortunately, it seems likely that the NBA will force these clubs to play all of their remaining games, so the fans, players, and staff are doomed to continue suffering until Spring.

(PA Media/dpa) - Jose Mourinho insists Real Madrid cannot afford to ease up as they prepare to host Alaves this weekend.

Mourinho's side will draw level with champions Barcelona at the top of LaLiga if they extend their winning run to seven matches with victory at the Bernabeu Stadium.

Real are also top of the Champions League standings after a thumping 5-1 comeback win over PSV Eindhoven in midweek, but head coach Mourinho is determined to keep their momentum going.

The Portuguese told reporters at a press conference on Friday: "I like the work Quique (Sanchez Flores) is doing with Alaves.

"They are in a comfortable position in the table and have a very clear identity and approach.

"Another difficult match awaits us but it's our third consecutive home game and we have been fully focused on winning all three, because every point not earned is a point lost, and they could be decisive.

"We have to go out there and try to secure all three points."

Mourinho confirmed England right-back Trent Alexander-Arnold was ruled out through illness but Ferland Mendy was in contention for the first time this season after a long lay-off with a thigh injury.

Two players certain to start are Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham, whose performances have made them almost impossible to leave out.

Mourinho said: "Mbappe has never been on the bench and Bellingham has only been there for one match.

"They play so many minutes not because of their status, but because of their performance. When one player's performance is on a level that no one else can match, that's what makes the difference."

England midfielder Bellingham has been in particularly good form this season and scored a stunning goal against PSV, but Mourinho did not want to be drawn into comparisons with the great Zinedine Zidane.

Mourinho also ruled out making changes to his squad in the January transfer window.

He said: "The squad is strong. There is no player here I do not want, nor would I open the door for anyone to leave. I do not want anyone to come nor anyone to leave."

Alaves, ninth in the table, travel to the Bernabeu boosted by claiming their first win in nine games with a 3-1 triumph over Deportivo La Coruna last weekend.

#2722. Treydan Stukes, Jermod McCoy, Las Vegas Raiders’ young defensive backs face Cleveland Browns’ young receiving corps in Week 12 key matchups

The Las Vegas Raiders' playoff chances have been freefalling recently, to the point where the Week 12 Sunday Night Football contest against the Cleveland Browns is a "must-win" to keep the Raiders' slim postseason hopes alive. That adds some extra importance to the key matchups below, and Las Vegas will be leaning heavily on several young players.

While Treydan Stukes has primarily lined up at free safety this season, the Raiders' coaching staff has been tapping into his versatility recently. According to Pro Football Focus, the second-round pick has recorded double-digit snaps in the box in seven of the last eight games and has 37 snaps as a slot corner during that time frame. Part of the reason for that is he's been tasked with covering tight ends.

Per Sumer Sports, Stukes' first target against a tight end came in Week 5, and he's been thrown at 13 times while guarding the position. That's yielded just nine catches for 46 yards (5.1 ypc) and a touchdown, on top of the defensive back recording an interception and three pass breakups. He especially turned heads against the San Francisco 49ers, giving up just two catches for nine yards to George Kittle, per PFF.

Meanwhile, tight end Harold Fannin Jr. leads the Browns in every major receiving category with 44 catches for 544 yards and four touchdowns. Those numbers are also fifth, sixth and tied for fourth at the position across the NFL, and Fannin ranks 12th with 1.63 yards per route run, according to PFF.

The second-year pro has been especially good after the catch. Among tight ends, he trails only Travis Kelce (375) with 320 YAC and is fourth with 7.3 YAC per reception. A big reason is that Fannin leads his position with 11 missed tackles forced. The good news for the Raiders is that Stukes has only missed three tackles at a 10.3 percent rate in coverage this season.

That sets up an interesting battle between two young, up-and-coming players in the league.

Vegas has played musical chairs at one of its two outside cornerback spots, giving starts to and rotating second-year pro Darien Porter Jr. and rookies Hezekiah Masses and Jermod McCoy week-by-week and throughout the game.

However, that trend stopped last week, when McCoy made his first NFL start and played 71 of the team's 73 defensive snaps. The plays he missed were short-yardage situations where the Raiders didn't have a corner on the field.

The Tennessee product certainly didn't have a perfect showing in Denver. He was targeted five times and yielded two catches for 55 yards, per PFF, with one of the incompletions coming via a drop where he was beaten deep. However, a lot of McCoy's bad reps were symptomatic of a player who just hasn't gotten much playing time, and he showed enough promise to, presumptively, hold down the starting spot for at least one more week. Most notably, he had an excellent rep against Broncos top receiver Jaylen Waddle to record a PBU.

The Raiders' problem is that the defense is also having issues at the other cornerback spot. Veteran Eric Stokes was supposed to be the team's shutdown corner but has already given up over 200 more yards in 2026 (460) than he did in all of 2025 (261), per PFF. That's in addition to an eight percent increase in completion percentage (56.0% to 64.2%) and three more touchdowns (one to four).

Porter and Masses have each had their moments this year, but neither has been consistent. The former is allowing a 56.5 completion percentage (13 catches on 23 targets) for 216 yards, no touchdowns and three forced incompletions but no interceptions. The latter's figures sit at 54.8 percent (17 for 31), 274 yards, five touchdowns and three forced incompletions, in addition to three picks.

Meanwhile, the Browns have a couple of impressive rookie receivers in KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston. The former has racked up 40 catches for 458 yards and a touchdown, while the latter has 33 grabs for 523 yards and three touchdowns. And the two wideouts complement each other well.

Concepcion is more of a chess piece who can be moved around, spending 63.4 percent of his pass snaps in the slot and 36.3 percent out wide, per PFF. A good amount of his production comes after the catch, where 245 or 53.5 percent of his yards have come, ranking ninth among receivers with 6.1 YAC per reception.

Boston, on the other hand, is a typical X-receiver type with 89.9 percent of his pass snaps coming on the outside. He's more of a downfield and contested catch threat, owning a 15.3-yard average depth of target and 10 contested catches (tied for 10th among wideouts) compared to Concepcion's 8.2 ADOT and two contested grabs.

So, two different flavors of receivers that are almost equally as effective, with Concepcion averaging 1.47 yards per route run and Boston right behind him at 1.41 yprr. That presents a difficult challenge for the Silver and Black's secondary, regardless of who's getting snaps at cornerback.

The Raiders' rushing attack had been pretty dormant for about two months, going seven weeks without registering 100 yards as a team until this past Sunday. The good news is the offense is coming off its best game on the ground, recording a season-high 143 rushing yards and 6.0 ypc.

Running backs Ashton Jeanty (11 carries, 79 yards and 7.2 ypc) and Mike Washington Jr. (nine carries, 42 yards and 4.7 ypc) finally had enough breathing room to be effective in the ground game. That's a testament to Vegas' offensive line, which has been searching all season for its best five and may have found it with rookie Trey Zuhn III getting the nod at right guard during the last four games.

But this week brings a new test for Las Vegas' ground game because Cleveland's linebackers, Quincy Williams and Carson Schwesinger, have been pretty good against the run this season.

Per PFF, Williams ranks tied for second at the position with 24 defensive stops against the run and is tied for eighth with a 9.7 percent run-stop rate. That's helped him post an 85.6 run defense grade, fourth-best among linebackers. Schwesinger doesn't have nearly as many impact tackles against the run with just eight run stops, but a 70.2 mark that ranks 30th is nothing to scoff at.

On top of this, the Raiders have leaned heavily on Jeanty in the passing game. He leads the team in receptions (51), is third in receiving yards (507) and is tied for second in receiving touchdowns (four). Additionally, those figures are second, first and tied for first among running backs across the NFL. In other words, the 2025 first-round pick will also test the Browns' linebackers as a receiver.

Williams' numbers in coverage are also impressive this season, giving up just 204 yards while recording three pass breakups and 13 stops. The latter two figures are tied for sixth and tied for 10th among linebackers. Meanwhile, Schewesinger has yielded a rather high 347 receiving yards with no forced incompletions, but is 11th in coverage snaps per reception allowed (12.2) and tied for seventh with 14 stops.

That adds extra importance to the running back-linebacker matchups this week, especially when it comes to Jeanty.

#2718. Another Year, Another Nightmare: Iowa 31 NEBRASKA 7

Different team. Same bumbling nonsense. But different results because those late field goal losses have now been replaced by a pair of consecutive, embarrassing drubbings.

Get ready for a week of renewed online rage while waiting for a bowl assignment that many national outlets are all but begging to be the Huskers vs. Central Florida – and you know who. A win may have boosted them into a higher-level match-up, but you can forget about that now.

When the Huskers took over following Iowa extendingto a 24-7 lead, they didn't seem to be moving with much urgency down three scores and allowing clock to run down. Colandrea mostly ran for his life and when 4th & 11 came, the Huskers went with a 7-yard pass to Luke Lindenmeyer and, naturally, the sure-tackling Hawkeyes brought him down a yard short effectively ending what little chance they had.

The first half ended with a pretty good deal of hope in the air. They had run the ball solidly and appeared to be doing well on both sides of the line. They started the 2nd half clicking by driving to the Iowa 13. Then, while spinning to his left to run or rollout, Anthony Colandrea lost the ball, Iowa recovered and ran it back the 29.

They failed to score, but Husker fans stomach's dropped realizing they had just taken 3-7 points off the board in a 3-point game.

The Huskers immediately went 3 & out, but the Colandrea fumble moment still seemed recoverable when the Hawkeyes immediately returned the favor by muffing a punt which Jamir Conn recovered. However, the Huskers went 3 & out again, came up short on a 4th down, and, at that point, basically choked out their death rattle.

They may end up scoring another, but I wasn't waiting until the gun to start writing this abomination.

And no injured starting quarterback or about-to-be-fired Defensive Coordinator to asterisk the blowout unlike the finishes to 2025. That winning the yardage battle for 11 straight games went out the window. The Iowa Hawkeyes simply came out for the second half with something the Huskers have yet to find in this rivalry to the tune of a 21-0 run.

Jamal Rule ran 17 times for 101 yards, but perhaps Iowa sacrificed a little there to make keeping Colandrea contained the priority. They did. Even with sack-adjusted totals, Colandrea managed only -2 yards on 4 carries. There were only 8 other runs besides those two, and I think the OR designation at running back can be removed with Rule now consistently getting the lion's share of the carries.

Defensively, surrendering 329 yards to Iowa doesn't sound awful, but they simply gave up too many chunk plays – and watching it happen through the air seemed surreal. This can't be pinned on the defense – they had three sacks and a whopping eight tackles for loss. But the offense once again put up a game where they appeared to have the ability to move the ball, but avoided points like Andy Dufresne avoiding the law on his run to Zihuatanejo.

As the clock wound down, one could see Iowa still pounding and scrapping for every yard, because these teams play every season, and the winner wants the loser to remember the pain.

While the 2026 tide seemed to turn in a positive way as far as competing with talented teams, the gap continues to weirdly be extending where the Hawkeyes are concerned. Iowa well and truly owns Nebraska at this point, and that's going to be the case until the Huskers just flat do something about it.

That day will come in the future at some point, but that day was not today.

#2717. Luka Doncic versus Victor Wembanyama: Buckle up for the MVP race

In one corner, there's the 6-foot-8 Slovenian superstar Luka Doncic who recently surpassed Michael Jordan for the best start in modern NBA history.

In the other, there's the 7-foot-4 Victor Wembanyama who's doing things on a basketball court that have never been done.

It's Luka Magic versus The Alien. It's offensive wizardry versus an inhuman skill set. It's a guy who uses pace and brakes to make himself unguardable versus a guy who seemingly flies above his competition.

And they're about to meet for the first time this season when the Lakers play the Spurs in San Antonio on Friday night.

Both of them would call this just another game. They'd be lying.

In tight MVP races, head-to-head contests are heavily weighed. This is a measuring stick game. There are implications that could resonate months later when awards voters make their decisions.

Doncic has been on a revenge tour since the Mavericks stunningly dealt him to the Lakers in February 2024, marking the first time in modern day NBA history that a player of his caliber in his prime was traded against his will.

Luka Doncic of the Los Angeles Lakers shoots a free throw against the Utah Jazz in Los Angeles on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images

Then there's Wembanyama, who's widely considered the next face of the league but ascended faster than anyone anticipated, carrying the Spurs to the 2026 NBA Finals. Once they arrived, his team unraveled.

The Spurs blew double-digit leads in all four of their losses to the Knicks, punctuated by allowing New York to claw its way back from a 29-point deficit in Game 4, the largest comeback in Finals history.

Wembanyama blamed himself. He was demoralized. Crestfallen.

Both Doncic and Wembanyama want to change the narrative. They each want to be MVP. They know they have to get through each other to accomplish their goal.

The 27-year-old Doncic has never finished higher than third in MVP award voting despite leading the league in scoring twice and carrying the Mavericks to the Finals in 2024.

The 22-year-old Wembanyama became the first ever unanimous Defensive Player of the Year and finished second in last year's MVP race behind Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.

San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama walks up court during an NBA basketball game against the New Orleans Pelicans on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026, in San Antonio. AP Photo/Darren Abate

Doncic is averaging a league-leading 36.6 points, 6.6 rebounds, 7.7 assists and 1.8 steals per game for the Lakers.

Wembanyama is averaging 29.9 points, 12.3 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 3.9 blocked shots for the Spurs.

Their teams have the two best records in the league, with LA 15-3 and San Antonio 15-4.

Doncic and Wembanyama are the it guys. They're dominating headlines. Dropping jaws. Taking over the narrative.

Doncic scored 40 or more points in four straight games. Wembanyama had a 50-point, 18-rebound and five-block performance against the Pelicans on Nov. 21. They're both putting up video game numbers.

Doncic all but refuses to advocate for himself for MVP. Wembanyama made the case for himself last season as though he were an attorney arguing in front of a jury.

Luka Doncic of the Los Angeles Lakers runs out before a game against the Utah Jazz on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images

But what Doncic won't say in words he has made clear with his actions. He wants this. Bad. He's playing more defense than ever in an attempt to dispel the negative narratives around him. He has already taken four charges this season.

Wembanyama wants this just as bad. And he's taking a different tack. He's leaning into the negative chatter. He turned into a villain (at least in New York) during the Finals. Instead of balking at that label, he told reporters he's choosing to view it as "a great sign of respect."

Both players have unique things fueling them and completely different styles, but they also have something very important in common.

They're sprinting next to each other for the most prestigious individual award in the sport.

And on Friday, we'll get our first glimpse of who's really in the lead.

#2716. Aaron Rodgers got no support from the Thanksgiving broadcasts

The day after former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers went on TV and aired dirty laundry from the Pittsburgh locker room, none of the former quarterbacks (or other former players) who appear on TV supported him.

Across the board, the reaction from the NFL’s analysts and broadcasters was negative.

Former Steelers quarterback and Fox analyst Terry Bradshaw went off. Fox’s Michael Strahan agreed that Rodgers shouldn’t have gone public with his complaints — calling him a “narcissist” and a “rich jerk” and a “rich bad teammate.”

Fox’s Howie Long said that the moment “defines who [Rodgers] is.”

“He’s a guy that I think picked the wrong sport,” Long said. “He probably should have played tennis.”

Fox’s Rob Gronkowski said that, even if a contender loses its starting quarterback, there’s “too much smoke” to justify bringing Rodgers in.

The CBS pregame crew offered similar views. Nate Burleson said Rodgers “didn’t handle this right.” Bill Cowher said he hates to see a Hall of Famer go out this way. Russell Wilson said, “It’s about Aaron Rodgers’s legacy. . . . If I’m his family members, if I’m somebody close to him, I’m his significant other, whatever it may be. ‘Is this how you want to go out?’ After all the success he’s had, is this how you want to go out? . . . This is a disappointment.”

During the Eagles-Cowboys game, Fox’s Tom Brady criticized Rodgers for violating the “sanctity” of the locker room.

The irony, if I’m using the term correctly (I never know), is that Rodgers has previously railed about leaks from the locker room.

“I think it’s chickenshit at its core, and I think it has no place in a winning organization,” Rodgers said about the Jets.

“One thing I really love — and it’s kind of the antithesis of where I was — is there’s not really any leaks in the boat,” Rodgers told reporters during his first year with the Steelers. “Every year, you have difficulties and adversity, both on the field and off the field, and to go through a season like this, and to be able to focus on football and not have a lot of other little bullshit out there has been really nice.”

Rodgers didn’t leak anything. He said it directly, bluntly, unapologetically. He took the team’s focus off of football, at a time when the team was otherwise trying to fight through “difficulties and adversity.”

Again, he isn’t a whistleblower. He’s a troublemaker. He didn’t get his way, so he set the house on fire as he walked out the front door.

As one PFT reader put it, ultimatums and “blackmail” are close cousins. For Rodgers, it wasn’t just “let me call the plays or cut me.” It was, whether he said it this way or not, “let me call the plays or I’ll tell the world all the stuff you don’t want the world to know.”

#2709. Fernando Mendoza found ‘something special’ in unlocking Raiders rising star

The first touchdown pass Fernando Mendoza threw in a Raiders uniform went to Jack Bech. It happened in a preseason game, so there was nothing particularly consequential about it in the grand scheme of things.

As it turns out, it might have been the first glimpse of something that could have lasting ramifications for the Raiders' offense.

A friendship that has blossomed away from the football field is beginning to manifest itself on it. And in the process, Mendoza might be helping unlock a player the Raiders invested a second-round pick in last year but have struggled to consistently incorporate into their offense.

Denver Broncos cornerback Riley Moss (21) tackles Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Jack Bech (18) during an NFL game in Denver, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/David Zalubowski

"Jack is a great guy. He's one of my best friends on the team," Mendoza said. "He's someone who's notorious for staying after practice and catching extra balls. He's been a fantastic player and teammate."

There is something to be said about the comfort level a quarterback develops with a receiver he spends time with away from the facility. Especially two young players navigating the early stages of their NFL careers and figuring out where they fit in the grand scheme of an organization.

What is becoming increasingly apparent is that Bech has a connection with Mendoza that he never seemed to establish with any of the other quarterbacks he has played with in Las Vegas.

And the implications of that extend well beyond the individual success of either player.

Consider what happened Sunday in Denver, when Bech caught eight passes on nine targets for 88 yards and a touchdown against one of the NFL's best defenses. Five of those catches produced first downs. Bech accounted for nearly half of Mendoza's 18 completions.

That is a pretty significant development for a young quarterback trying to find his footing in the NFL and a young wide receiver trying to establish his value in it.

And none of it surprised Raiders coach Klint Kubiak.

"Well, I think a quarterback and receiver relationship builds when there's adverse times and the guys are making plays," Kubiak said. "So, those plays that Jack made last night, those are things that he's done in practice with Fernando. He has the trust of the quarterback."

It's important to understand something about Bech as the Raiders continue constructing an offense around Mendoza.

He might never develop into the legitimate No. 1 wide receiver Raiders fans are clamoring for. He might not even fit the traditional description of a No. 2 receiver.

But that doesn't mean he can't be an immensely valuable piece of a championship-caliber offense.

Think of a bigger-bodied, more physical version of Hunter Renfrow in terms of situational value. Someone who understands leverage, finds soft spots in coverage, operates effectively in congested areas and becomes almost instinctively aligned with his quarterback.

The guy Mendoza looks for on third-and-7. The guy he trusts to come down with a contested catch in the end zone. The guy who understands where he needs to be when a play breaks down.

Factor in Bech's special teams contributions and the physicality and willingness he brings as a blocker in the run game, and it's easy to envision him becoming the type of player coaches struggle to take off the field.

Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) throws against the Denver Broncos in Denver, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/Jack Dempsey

Kubiak has consistently pointed out how much you can feel Bech's physicality.

"He's always been gritty, always been a great teammate," Kubiak said. "Then you get opportunities against a really good defense, and he made plays. So I'm happy for him. I'm not surprised."

Great football teams aren't exclusively populated by star football players. They're supplemented by capable, dependable role players who understand precisely what is required of them and consistently deliver.

That distinction sometimes gets lost in our obsession with draft positions, depth charts and statistical production.

If Bech becomes that kind of player, nobody should apologize for the Raiders using a second-round pick on him.

Especially if he develops alongside Mendoza over the next several years, complementing the star power of Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty and whatever high-end receiving talent the Raiders eventually add.

Bech, interestingly, deflects attention from his individual relationship with Mendoza to emphasize the broader connection the rookie quarterback has established throughout the locker room.

"Not only has he gotten better on the field from April, but the way he's just taking that leadership role," Bech said. "We all have faith and confidence in him."

Mendoza, meanwhile, traces his connection with Bech back to that preseason touchdown.

"Even though it was a preseason game, it's still a great game, and at that moment I realized that we had something special," Mendoza said.

Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak speaks during a news conference after an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos in Denver, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/David Zalubowski

What makes their friendship particularly intriguing is that neither appears inclined to take the football component of it for granted. There are extra passes to throw and catch after practice, nuances to master and a level of trust to continue earning.

The Raiders drafted Mendoza to be the face of their franchise.

If his arrival also helps Bech become one of the foundational pieces surrounding him, that would represent a pretty significant bonus.

#2707. Nets vs. Raptors Preview: Can Brooklyn capitalize against a shorthanded Toronto team?

DETROIT, MI – NOVEMBER 20: Scottie Barnes #4 of the Toronto Raptors celebrates in the final minute of a win over the Detroit Pistons at Little Caesars Arena on November 20, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Duane Burleson/Getty Images) | Getty Images

A much needed victory. The Brooklyn Nets continued their road trip with a matchup against the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday night. Brooklyn got back into the win column with a 104-97 win and hopes that it can be the start of a much-needed turnaround.

The Toronto Raptors are coming off perhaps their most frustrating loss of the season — a 116-111 loss at the hands of the lowly Milwaukee Bucks. That's a team the Nets just snapped their own five-game losing streak against. Toronto will be missing Kawhi Leonard and RJ Barrett in this one, so the Nets should really find a way to squeeze out with a win.

Who: Brooklyn Nets (4-13) vs. Toronto Raptors (6-11)

OUT – Nolan Traore (right hamstring strain)

OUT – Mo Wagner (left knee injury management)

OUT – Kawhi Leonard (left knee injury management)

OUT – RJ Barrett (right hamstring strain)

QUESTIONABLE – Alijah Martin (left knee soreness)

The Brooklyn Nets (4-13) travel north to face the Toronto Raptors (6-11) on Friday night in the front end of an international back-to-back. Once this one wraps up, they're flying back to the States for a matchup in Charlotte Hornets on Saturday night.

Ben Saraf was called up to the big club, so we'll see how Jordi Fernandez utilizes him. Mikel Brown Jr. has yet to play both ends of a back-to-back, but with Traore out, Brooklyn's guard room has even less margin for error. Brown Jr. will have to start playing both ends of a back-to-back eventually, so now would be a perfect time to start.

We expected a lot more from the Raptors this year, but circumstances have gotten in the way. Kawhi Leonard has only appeared in two games this season, though he is doing individual workouts and hopes to be back soon enough. In the meantime, the team will have to make do without the former NBA Finals MVP. From Julian Apolinario of Raptors HQ:

"Unfortunately, the Raptors look like they're not constructed in a way that they can win big games without Kawhi Leonard, at least, not yet. It's early in the season, and there are more games ahead of the Raptors than behind them, and given some more time with a clear starting lineup, the Raptors might be able to put it together.

A machine doesn't work while missing its biggest gear, and it seems that no matter how well the Raptors play, they remain a step behind the best teams in the league. Come playoff time, things will have to be different if the Raps want any real chance of success this year, but that doesn't necessarily mean that things are hopeless with the current roster — injuries just need to be on their side."

Michael Porter Jr. is still working through his slump. The Nets forward has been under 45 percent shooting from the field in four consecutive games and for a team that needs his scoring to be close to competitive, they can't afford extended cold stretches from him. Every day is a chance to get back on the good foot, so the Nets hope today is the day MPJ returns to his All-Star caliber form.

It wasn't supposed to be like this, but we're learning something exciting along the way. With Leonard and Barrett on the team, Scottie Barnes was not expected to be the focal point of the team's offense. However, with those two out, he's had to take on more of the scoring and playmaking responsibilities to keep the team afloat. Barnes is at career highs in usage rate, field goal attempts, and points per game. Also, he's been living in the midrange area a lot more as he's at career lows in three-point attempt rate and percentage of shots attempted inside of three feet. Barnes is a tremendous finisher at the rim so it'll be interesting to see how Toronto finds him more opportunities near the basket.

Julius Randle will draw the Barnes matchup and see if he can continue his recent shooting success. Randle has shot at least 45 percent from the field in nine out of the last ten games, and the Nets will need that to continue tonight. When Randle is assertive and making good decisions, the ceiling for the Nets offense is a lot higher. When he holds on to the ball too much, things get stagnant and frustrations rise.

Even shorthanded, the Raptors pose an interesting challenge for the Nets and we'll see how the team does on the front end of a back-to-back.

#2687. Patriots Must Skip Daniel Jones As Maye Sits Out

The New England Patriots need a quarterback fast, but signing Daniel Jones is a trap. The 5-5 squad just lost two straight games by a combined 43 points. His stats have taken a massive dive since his last big contract. He has managed only 8 touchdowns while throwing 13 interceptions in 11 games this year. That is a terrible ratio for a team trying to climb back into the playoff mix.

In 2025, Jones joined the Colts and initially performed brilliantly. A 7-1 start saw him guide the team until a torn Achilles cut short his season. But his play has regressed badly since he returned. This year he has reached 250 yards only two times, whereas last season he exceeded 250 yards in over half of his games. His completion rate fell by nearly 10 percentage points. The Patriots cannot afford a backup who is struggling this hard. The team already has Tommy DeVito and rookie Behren Morton to fill in.

Drake Maye is not on injured reserve, even though he is out for at least six weeks. Head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed the status on Monday. "I think right now, he's not on the reserve list, he's not on injured reserve," Vrabel said. Maye suffered a hairline fracture in his fibula during the Week 10 loss to the Detroit Lions. He has not been spotted at practice this week, but he is still in the building. Rookie Behren Morton told the Boston Herald that Maye is still active in meetings. "He was chiming in during meetings, which is always helpful," Morton said.

"Drake's a good dude, and he's texting both Tommy (DeVito) and I whatever we need. You know he's going to be here for us," Morton said. This support system is better than bringing in a veteran who might disrupt the locker room. The Patriots have other issues to fix, like a defense that allowed 80 points in consecutive losses. Defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr has a clear plan to fix those mistakes now.

Fans might wonder if Aaron Rodgers is an option, but that is a fantasy. NFL insider Mike Garafolo said there are no talks for Rodgers. "We're looking at potentially New England … New England has shown no inclination to move in that direction," Garafolo said. Rodgers has burned too many bridges and his play has dropped off. He is missing checkdowns and sacking himself.

He is on the active roster so the team can try to give him every opportunity to return. The Patriots face the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 4:05 p.m. ET at SoFi Stadium. That game is the next step in a tough stretch that includes the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings.

#2678. Luka Dončić says he asked Lakers front office to acquire Walker Kessler: "I went to them and said, 'I want Walker"'

One of the Los Angeles Lakers' biggest offseason moves is paying off big so far — and Luka Dončić is taking a bit of credit for making it happen.

Lakers center Walker Kessler, who was acquired from the Utah Jazz in a sign-and-trade deal in July, has been a key piece of the team on both ends of the court so far this season. And as it turns out, Dončić told ESPN's Dave McMenamin that he played a role in Kessler's arrival in L.A.

In McMenamin's profile on Kessler published Friday, Dončić said that he spoke to Rob Pelinka, the Lakers' president of basketball operations and general manager, during the offseason about acquiring the big man from the Jazz. Dončić said that he was inspired by Kessler's impressive defense at the rim after playing against him in previous seasons.

"I told them after the season I wanted Walker," Dončić told ESPN, speaking about that offseason conversation. "I think he's a really good player … Obviously, last season he didn't play. He played like five games. Obviously [Utah] kept him out, but just playing against him in the previous years, it was hard to score. He was protecting the rim, he was dominating the paint. So just after the season, I went to them and said, 'I want Walker.'"

Dončić credits his burgeoning chemistry with Kessler as a key piece of the team's growth. When speaking about his pick-and-roll with Kessler, Dončić told ESPN: "When we get good at that … we can be really good."

In response, Kessler told ESPN that he was honored to have Dončić want him as a teammate.

"To have someone like that, with that pedigree, to say, 'Hey, I want that to be our center'... it was incredible," Kessler said. "I was like, 'Wow, this dude, he believes in me. He knows that I can help this team.' It makes you excited to play."

In many ways, the Kessler trade was risky: The Lakers sent two unprotected first-round picks (2031 and 2033) and two first-round swaps (2028 and 2030) for the 25-year-old big man, who only played in five games last year after undergoing season-ending shoulder surgery in November 2025.

But so far, the move has paid off. Kessler is averaging team-leading 10.8 rebounds and 2.1 blocks per game, and is the Lakers' third-highest scorer with 14 points per game. His 66.9% field-goal percentage is one of the best in the NBA.

It's not a huge surprise that Dončić, who is the Lakers' last remaining superstar after the offseason departure of LeBron James, has filled in the role of player-GM. Dončić is the face of the team and the leading scorer, and seems to have gained significant influence in the Lakers front office.

After the Kessler trade went through in July, Dončić said at the time that he was "excited" about the addition. Reports at the time indicated that the team was following Dončić's two biggest requests, which were to retain Austin Reaves (who signed a four-year, $185 million extension this summer) and bring in a rim protector like Kessler.

The trio of Dončić, Reaves and Kessler have led the Lakers to a 15-3 record to start the season, putting them at the top of the Western Conference.

#2677. Ryan Fitzpatrick says criticism of Broncos QB Bo Nix 'crossed a line'

Editor's note: Follow live coverage of the Denver Broncos vs. Pittsburgh Steelers Black Friday game here.

The day after Thanksgiving game came with a side of crow for Amazon Prime Video NFL analyst Ryan Fitzpatrick.

Prime Video host Charissa Thompson sat down with Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix prior to the Nov. 27 Black Friday game between the Broncos and Pittsburgh Steelers. After the piece aired, Thompson reminded Fitzpatrick that he was critical of Nix after Denver's Oct. 15 victory over the Seattle Seahawks on "Thursday Night Football."

"I know you two have squashed it," Thompson said. "You got on the phone. You talked, so that's over."

Nix was in his sixth game back after fracturing his ankle in a January divisional-round playoff game and completed 17 of 27 passes for 107 yards. He ran four times for 2 yards. He regularly passed up passes down the field and instead threw the ball out of bounds or took a sack. It was the fourth week in a row the Denver offense had totaled less than 300 yards; Nix averaged 4.0 yards per attempt.

The 2024 first-round pick has certainly played better since then. He's thrown 6 touchdowns in the last four contests and has taken one sack per game in that span.

The Broncos are 6-0 since head coach Sean Payton took over play calling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb.

"Going back to that, I did have some harsh critiques of him. I felt like – it did feel like it crossed a line into being personal and so that's why I reached out to him, and just said 'Look, I'm sorry, it wasn't a personal attack.' You see, he looks like the nicest person in the world there with his family," Fitzpatrick said, alluding to the Thompson interview.

It was quite the different tone from what he said after the win over the Seahawks. Fitzpatrick's postgame rant went viral and was striking since it was a former NFL quarterback being particularly harsh on one of his own brethren.

"It was really frustrating to watch," Fitzpatrick said. "Bo Nix is not playing competitively, it's almost disrespectful to the quarterback position how he's playing football.

"First of all, the guy doesn't want to throw the ball," Fitzpatrick continued, bemoaning Nix's decision-making on the aborted Denver drive late in the fourth quarter that gave Seattle the opportunity to tie the game and force overtime.

#2672. Iowa, not SEC bias, is Indiana's biggest College Football Playoff problem

Indiana would like to make its playoff pickle about the selection committee and SEC bias.

That's red meat to fire up the Hoosiers' ravenous base, but it misses the point.

Iowa is the problem. Oregon is the problem. UCLA is the problem.

CFP rankings live predictions: How will Big Ten chaos affect Playoff bracket?

The Hoosiers' path to the playoff remains blocked, because, even in a down year for the Big Ten, the committee likes a few Big Ten teams better than the defending national champions.

If the committee decides to select a 10-2 Big Ten team as its last-team-in, that team will be Iowa, not Indiana.

It became harder to argue with the committee's preference for Iowa after the No. 13 Hawkeyes thrashed Nebraska, 31-7, in a rivalry game, one week after the Huskers beat Ohio State.

Iowa joins Oregon as the Big Ten's hottest teams.

If the committee wants the nation's top-rated scoring defense in the bracket, then it must make room for the Hawkeyes.

Turns out, Nebraska's win against Ohio State was not a Matt Rhule breakthrough. It was a mirage, and the Huskers regained their theme music by losing to a ranked opponent, complete with two turnovers by quarterback Anthony Colandrea.

"Great job" by the defense, Iowa coach Kirk Ferentz told CBS at halftime.

His defense looked even better in the second half.

Iowa is essentially Indiana with a superior ground game and without the quarterback controversy. Hank Brown delivered his best performance in weeks. His fourth-quarter touchdown pass pushed Iowa one step closer to the bracket, and put Indiana's hopes on life support. Brown also rushed for three scores.

For Iowa, consider Brown a quarterback revelation. Iowa has scored at least 24 points in every game of its five-game win streak.

This is not the three-runs-and-punt Iowa of yeseteryear.

You won't confuse these Hawkeyes with 2019 LSU or 2020 Alabama or 2025 Indiana, but you also won't confuse them with 2023 Iowa.

A week ago, a reporter gave Ferentz a platform to make Iowa's case to the committee. He demurred.

"I swear to God, I could care less about (the committee)," Ferentz told the Big Ten Network. "They're gonna do what they want to do, and I really don't care."

Yep, that sounds like Ferentz. He stuck to that tune after beating Nebraska.

"I'm just happy we won today," Ferentz told CBS. "We weren't thinking about (the playoff)."

The committee liked Iowa enough to give it the No. 13 spot in its latest rankings, sandwiched between No. 12 Oregon and No. 14 Indiana.

With a dash of chaos on rivalry Saturday, the Hawkeyes could climb enough in the rankings to nab the final at-large spot.

Or, Iowa still could take this out of the committee's hands. If either UCLA or Oregon loses its rivalry game on Saturday, the Hawkeyes will nab a spot in the Big Ten championship, with an automatic bid on the line.

If Curt Cignetti needs someone to blame for Indiana's playoff predicament, start with Iowa. The Hawkeyes are a roadblock that refused to be moved.

As the final seconds wound off the clock at Kinnick Stadium, the CBS cameras found a fan in the stands holding a sign reading, Put Iowa in the CFP.

The Hawkeyes' playoff credentials are better than they've ever been after this romp, and Indiana simultaneously moved another step toward the edge of the plank.

Karl-Anthony Towns was downgraded to questionable with an abdominal contusion, Andre Drummond is out in concussion protocol and OG Anunoby is out with a calf strain. Giannis Antetokounmpo is probable with groin tendinitis, Austin Reaves is back from a heel bruise and De'Aaron Fox is questionable with a shin injury.

Using Yahoo projections, each player's last five games, the betting lines and the latest injury news, I ran 20,000 simulations of the slate against a simulated Yahoo field built from this week's pick rates. I'm pairing the two best fantasy players on the board and spreading the rest of the lineup across all four teams, so I have a stake in every game.

This group finished in the top 1% of the simulated field 23.4% of the time and beat every entry in the field in 1.49% of sims, and nobody in the simulated field had these exact five. It holds up whether Towns plays or not: 24.3% of the time in the sims where he played and 21.6% when he sat.

Wembanyama is the top projection on the board at 58.17 fantasy points. Over his last five games, he's averaged about 68 fantasy points, including 50 points, 18 rebounds, 4 steals and 5 blocks against the Pelicans last Friday, and 44 points with 16 rebounds at Portland on Wednesday. The blocks are what separate him: he's averaging 3.8 a game, and every one is worth three points.

You'll want some star exposure in a matchup featuring two of the NBA's best teams. San Antonio is a 6.5-point home favorite, and the 226.5 total is the higher of the two games. Wemby was in the single best lineup in 58% of my sims, more than anyone else. Yes, 61% of the field has him, but fading a player this far ahead of everyone else isn't worth it.

This is the pick that makes the lineup. Giannis is projected for 53.67 fantasy points, essentially even with Luka Dončić, but he's on 7% of rosters to Dončić's 58%. He's been a beast in Miami — scoring about 59 fantasy points a game over his last five, including 34 points, 14 rebounds, 8 assists, and 3 blocks against Detroit, and 32 points and 14 rebounds at Philadelphia on Wednesday.

He came into this game probable with a groin injury, but that shouldn't be an issue since he played 36 minutes against Philly a couple of days ago. And the Knicks' frontcourt looks weaker than usual: Drummond is out, Anunoby is doubtful and Towns is a game-time call.

Thybulle is the next best defensive-stats play on the slate to Wemby. He's averaging 2.3 steals and a block, and he's turned that into about 26 fantasy points a game over his last five, with at least 2 steals in four of them. He's added some offense too, scoring 14 points in each of his last two games. Reaves's return could trim his minutes a little, but his value comes from defense, not shots, and that holds up even in a smaller role.

Shamet gets this lineup into the early game without paying for a Knicks star whose status is up in the air (Towns). Shamet's averaging about 19 fantasy points over his last five, right on his 19.50 projection. He's played 30-plus minutes in three of his last four games. He should be in more Sixth Man of the Year conversations and, at 11% picked, he's also a cheaper way to get leverage than Klay Thompson, who's on 58% of rosters at the same $2 cost.

Conwell is the value that makes two $5 stars work. He's projected for 19.25 fantasy points at $1, the best points-per-dollar mark on the slate, and he's played 25-30 minutes in four of his last five games. He doesn't need a big night; 15 to 20 fantasy points from your $1 slot is plenty. He showed up in the optimal lineup in 51% of my sims, more than any player except Wembanyama. The rookie is gaining confidence by the game, so I'll keep riding the wave.

Dončić is projected for 53.95 fantasy points, but that number was built during a stretch where he's carried the Lakers by himself. Reaves is back Friday after missing five games, and some of the shots and touches Dončić has been soaking up will go back to his running mate. I trimmed his projection about 5% in the sims to account for that. Even at full strength, he'd be a tough sell: he costs the same $5 as Giannis, projects for about the same and is on eight times as many rosters.

Very close. Using Yahoo's projections, the highest-scoring possible lineup is Wembanyama, Dončić, Thompson, Thybulle and Conwell at 173.75 fantasy points. Mine comes in just 2.04 points behind it.

The max lineup finished in the top 1% only about 12% of the time, roughly half my lineup's rate. Swapping Dončić for Giannis and Thompson for Shamet gives up two projected points and gets you out of the game's most crowded build.

You can start building your Perfect 5 roster for Friday's slate now, including going up against me in my Perfect 5 group.

#2668. Tony Gonzalez, Ryan Fitzpatrick tee off on ‘selfish’ Aaron Rodgers after Steelers mess

Prime Video analysts didn't mince words when dissecting Aaron Rodgers' rant — and subsequent divorce — from the Steelers this week.

Ahead of the Steelers' game against the Broncos on Black Friday, the pregame show opened with a segment about Rodgers' benching, his now-infamous interview on "The Pat McAfee Show," his scathing accusations of Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy and his release Wednesday afternoon.

Hall of Famer Tony Gonzalez called Rodgers "selfish" and former quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick added that Rodgers will be remembered as "one of the most complicated athletes of all time."

"It's sad," Gonzalez said. "It's really sad for everybody. … It makes no sense. You're talking out of two sides of your mouth. What you're saying, it's insane the way Mike McCarthy is acting, but you're the one who vouched for him to come over here, to get him into the building. And then you nuke everybody. You nuke your teammates, a playoff football team. I just think it makes no sense. It's one of those things that's gonna go down in history."

Aaron Rodgers of the Pittsburgh Steelers reacts against the Philadelphia Eagles in Philadelphia on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. The Eagles won 19-16. Getty Images

Fitzpatrick said that the Steelers' locker room is like a chess board for Rodgers, where all the pieces are "expendable" when they "can't protect the king."

"He is loved by his teammates wherever he's been," Fitzpatrick said. "And this Pittsburgh Steelers locker room, they loved Aaron Rodgers and the teammate that he is. But the complicated part is what did he do? He blew everything up. He sees the locker room like a chess board, is what I feel like.

Amazon Prime Video host Ryan Fitzpatrick appears on the pregame show before a game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Denver Broncos, Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

"All the pieces that he can manipulate and move, they're very precious to him as long as they're protecting the king, but as soon as they don't have value and they can't protect the king, then all of a sudden, they become expendable — and he throws them out. And this is what happened with Mike McCarthy."

Tension between Rodgers — who was in his second year with the Steelers — and McCarthy dated back to their years with the Packers, but it boiled over again this week.

Despite two consecutive losses, McCarthy stood by Rodgers as his quarterback Monday. Then, one day later, the Steelers dropped a press release at 11:10 p.m. that named Mason Rudolph the starter for Friday's home tilt.

And one day later, Rodgers returned to McAfee's show and proceeded to shred McCarthy, claiming that the longtime NFL head coach fell asleep in meetings and broke down a halftime huddle Sunday with "1-2-3 Packers."

Amazon Prime Video host Tony Gonzalez speaks on the pregame show before a game in Pittsburgh, Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

The Steelers, via owner Art Rooney II, have reiterated their full support for McCarthy, who admitted to the Packers blunder, didn't deny the sleeping allegations during his session with reporters Wednesday and said Rodgers' "ultimatum" led to Pittsburgh cutting ties with the signal-caller.

Even with their recent pair of losses, the Steelers only sit a game behind the Bengals in the AFC North, and they'll now turn to Rudolph as their starter after releasing Rodgers.

And even though Rodgers cleared waivers, Prime Video insider James Palmer reported on Friday's pregame show that there's "little to no interest" from teams in signing the 42-year-old and four-time NFL MVP — whose storied career on the field just took its latest turn away from it.

"I've never seen anything like this in my life," Gonzalez said, "and we've played this game for a long time. And just not in football. Basketball, hockey, it is unprecedented what went on, and it's one of those things — it's like a little hint of narcissism … to come out on air on 'The Pat McAfee Show' and do what he did."

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

#2663. Royce Lewis trade grades: Dodgers land former No. 1 pick; Twins get another arm, arrow-up prospect

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Los Angeles Dodgers have added a former No. 1 overall pick. The Dodgers are set to acquire infielder Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins for right-hander Bobby Miller and minor-league catcher Francisco Espinoza, reports the New York Post. Neither team has announced the trade.

Lewis, 27, was a candidate to be non-tendered prior to Friday's deadline. Rather than cut him loose, the Twins were able to find a trade partner and receive something in return. The No. 1 pick in the 2017 draft has battled injuries throughout his career and posted a .288 on-base percentage the last three years. Lewis simply failed to launch with Minnesota.

The Dodgers figure to use Lewis as a platoon partner for Max Muncy at third base and could also move him around the infield as a utility guy. The Twins moved him from third base to first base this past season. Lewis has played every infield position in the big leagues, though he's had only one inning at shortstop since 2022.

Miller, 27, has been unable to build on his dynamic 2022 rookie season, when he threw 124 ⅓ innings with a 3.76 ERA. He has battled injuries and control issues since then, and the Dodgers moved him into the bullpen this past season. Miller has a 7.75 ERA in 134 ⅔ Triple-A innings the last three years and can be optioned down in 2027.

Espinoza, 19, reached Low Class-A in 2026 and hit .317/.411/.422 with three home runs and strong contact rates in 46 games. He does not rank among the top 30 Dodgers prospects at Baseball America or MLB Pipeline, but Espinoza is an arrow-up prospect and a solid return for a non-tender candidate.

Here now are our grades for the two-for-one trade.

At worst, Lewis will be a high-priced utility guy next season. He's projected to make $5 million or so through arbitration and that simply is not much for the Dodgers, who have a history of getting underperforming hitters to the next level (like Muncy). At best, Lewis could be the new Chris Taylor and reach his offensive ceiling while bouncing between positions.

Espinoza is a good prospect, not a great prospect, and Miller is a reclamation project. Those are easy players for the Dodgers to surrender to take a chance on Lewis and his upside. It may not work. Lewis could continue to get hurt and not hit, but it was a low-cost move and the chance of a reward is significant.

It's a very nice upside play for a team that has hit on a lot of upside plays over the year.

It's a bummer things didn't work out for Lewis and the Twins, but the reality is he was a non-tender candidate, and it wasn't a secret. Minnesota was able to get back a solid prospect in Espinoza and a lottery ticket arm in Miller despite having little leverage. Getting two players for Lewis is a very good outcome under the circumstances.

Giving each team an "A" suggests a win-win, and maybe it will be. There's a chance it's a lose-lose, though. Lewis may not hit, Miller may never rediscover his 2022 form, and Espinoza may not pan out. I see the vision for both teams, though and like it.

The Dodgers rolled the dice on a talented player and the Twins were able to fetch two players for someone they might have otherwise cut loose and sent into free agency.

And this matchup is bound to deliver plenty of fireworks — even if not for the actual football being played on the field.

It was a week full of drama for the Steelers, as the team was sent reeling following a Week 11 upset by the Philadelphia Eagles, leading to the benching of future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers in favor of backup Mason Rudolph. The drama didn't end there, as Rodgers went scorched earth on Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy in an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" Wednesday after his benching, leveling a series of accusations toward his now-former coach, eventually leading to his release.

The Steelers sit at 6-4 and would be the No. 7 seed in the AFC playoffs if the season were to end today. So now, they must move forward with Rudolph as McCarthy attempts to wrangle in the chaos released in the locker room after this week's events in an attempt to maintain that playoff positioning.

The Broncos, meanwhile, sit at 8-2 in first place in the AFC West, all but locked into a playoff spot, and now with some cushion after the Kansas City Chiefs fell to the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving. After a slow start to the season, the offense has made some improvements since head coach Sean Payton resumed play calling, scoring 26-plus points in each of their past four matchups.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Broncos and Steelers face off in a special Black Friday showdown in Week 12.

On third down, Nick Herbig gets to Bo Nix in the backfield for a big 12-yard loss. Herbig, who missed last week's game with multiple injuries, has had several key plays today in his return.

That was Denver's best drive yet, with the Broncos getting up to eight plays after failing to convert in their first three drives, but it ends in another disappointment.

The Steelers capitalize on their hot start: With a 22-yard throw, Mason Rudolph finds DK Metcalf just in front of the goal line, with the receiver leaping and landing against the pylon.

That's a bit of redemption for Metcalf, who was ejected last week after multiple altercations with Cooper DeJean of the Eagles. Pittsburgh now takes a 14-0 lead as the quarter winds down.

On the first play of the Steelers' next drive, Mason Rudolph finds Germie Bernard down the middle, with the rookie receiver finding the space for a big gain — and nearly outrunning the Broncos all the way to the end zone.

What a tackle from Nick Herbig to deny Denver a conversion on third-and-inches! Jonah Coleman takes the carry, and tries to go around the scrum to cross the first-down line, but Herbig holds Coleman back from the edge to force a Broncos punt.

After three drives, Denver has yet to convert a first down so far in this game.

Pittsburgh's defense comes up big after putting big pressure on Bo Nix. As Nix scrambles backwards, T.J. Watt sacks Nix and forces the Denver quarterback to fumble. As the ball goes into the end zone, Watt is able to get there and smother it for a touchdown.

Denver gets the stop after Nik Bonitto gets Mason Rudolph in the backfield for a 13-yard loss. Rudolph had time while looking for an open receiver, but the Broncos secondary did a great job of covering those outlets before Rudolph was taken down.

Quick three-and-out for the Broncos, after back-to-back incomplete passes from Bo Nix.

A solid start for the Steelers, who pick up two first-downs but can't quite convert to keep the drive going. Pittsburgh has a chance to go for it, or at least go for the field goal, on fourth-and-3 at the Denver 43, but Mike McCarthy opts to punt instead.

McCarthy and the Steelers appear to be relying on the run game early in this matchup, likely due to a combination of the new starting quarterback and the cold, windy weather.

Black Friday football is now underway! Mason Rudolph and the Steelers get started with the ball on a rainy holiday in Pittsburgh.

There is a laundry list of reasons why other teams would not sign the man who just aired quite a bit of dirty laundry.

And yet: NFL teams have operated off far less logical desperation before. Rodgers' arm strength has not fully dissipated, nor has his line-of-scrimmage command lost its argument among the best in the game.

So multiple sources weren't ready to fully rule out a Rodgers return to the NFL this season.

#2657. Commanders to be without top cornerback vs. Cardinals

Washington Commanders cornerback Amik Robertson injured his ankle on the final play of last week's practice. The Commanders didn't play until Monday, so there was hope that Robertson could play. Robertson was on the field with Washington's training staff before the game but was clearly in pain and was ruled out of the game against the 7-2 Cincinnati Bengals.

This week, the Commanders face the Arizona Cardinals. It's a short week and a West Coast trip. Robertson did not practice all week, and Washington ruled him out on Friday before the team boarded a plane headed west.

Head coach Dan Quinn opened his Friday press conference by ruling Robertson out.

"One player who won't be able to play is Amik, and he's working his ass off to get back," Quinn said. "He's just not there yet. And so still dealing with an ankle. So, all that said, glad to get rolling with you guys."

Is Quinn concerned about a potential long-term issue with Robertson's injury?

"We're not there yet. Just like a lot of ankle injuries, like he's working as hard as he can; just hasn't turned it yet. He's frustrated where we all are for him, but, man, is he competing to battle for it. But no, we've not had any long-term discussions."

With Robertson out, the Commanders faced Cincinnati's top-ranked passing attack and held the potent duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins to under 80 combined receiving yards. Rasul Douglas stepped up in a pivotal role, and Washington's pass rush made life difficult for Joe Burrow.

The Commanders face the Tennessee Titans in Week 13, and hope Robertson will be ready by then, or they could play it safe for a few weeks. It's unknown if Robertson is dealing with a high ankle sprain, which is more serious than a low ankle sprain.

#2652. Former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin on Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy saga: 'It's a dumpster fire'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Pittsburgh Steelers are facing a unique kind of adversity as they prepare for their "Black Friday" matchup against the Denver Broncos. Late Tuesday night, the team announced it was benching future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph. On Wednesday, Rodgers appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" and lashed out against Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy. That led to his release.

Rodgers' attack of his head coach felt personal and unprecedented. On national television, he accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings, not putting in the work required to prepare for upcoming opponents, and failing to connect with players in his first season as the lead man in Pittsburgh. The breaking point, according to Rodgers, was when McCarthy, 63, broke down the team saying, "1-2-3 Packers!" at halftime of Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. McCarthy last coached the Packers in 2018. The coach admitted using the wrong team name during a press conference on Wednesday.

Fans and former players have not been shy in voicing their opinions on this wild saga, but one man we all wanted to hear from about this situation was Mike Tomlin. The new NBC analyst spent 19 years as the head coach of the Steelers, winning Super Bowl XLIII with the franchise in 2009. He famously never registered a losing season with the Steelers, and coached Rodgers during his final year as coach in 2025. During halftime of the Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills matchup on Thanksgiving, he revealed what he thought about Rodgers' actions in an interview with Mike Tirico.

Tomlin said he had a range of emotions hearing what Rodgers had to say about his new head coach, but the prevailing emotion was "general sadness."

"Sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career in the quarterback Aaron Rodgers, and just at the macro level whether it's organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum," Tomlin said. "Those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football."

Did it shock Tomlin that Rodgers went this route?

"It certainly did," Tomlin said. "Particularly because I know both men involved. [I] certainly had a lot of intimate work and development of relationships with Aaron over the last couple of years and have known and competed with Mike and respected and appreciated him as a coach for a long time."

Tomlin was asked how Rodgers was viewed in the locker room during his one year in Pittsburgh.

"He was beloved, and I'm not over-exaggerating that," Tomlin said. "He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness to getting to know and understand the Steeler culture. To be engaged with teammates, and particularly from my perspective, I worked with a lot of veteran players over the years and at times they lose a little patience for the process or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys, etcetera. Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real natural way."

Tomlin was asked whether McCarthy can effectively lead this team for the rest of the season?

"You know it certainly created some challenges and 'challenges' is probably an understatement if all of those things are true. Certainly, the '1-2-3 Packers' is because he acknowledged that. But his ability to overcome that or inability to overcome that in my opinion is based on relationships, and the depth of those relationships and how those guys feel about him or how those guys buy into what he's selling. And so certainly he's been there a short period of time, and so it makes you wonder the level of that challenge. But it will be relationship-based, his ability to overcome the things that you mentioned."

Tirico asked Tomlin what his emotions were being a coach that was involved with the Steelers franchise for nearly two decades

"I'm upset about it, it's a dumpster fire," Tomlin said. "And I don't say that in a judgemental way; I've presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. But it certainly is upsetting, and I'm sure Steeler Nation is upset."

There were plenty of bewildering aspects of this story. Tom Pelissero reported that frustration had been building behind the scenes among some players and coaches about Rodgers, who was calling plays himself. The quarterback reportedly went to McCarthy and demanded more changes related to the play-calling process. The coach received feedback from players and coaches indicating that's not what they wanted. Rodgers then issued an ultimatum: "Run things my way, or I quit."

ESPN's Brooke Pryor also reported that "multiple league sources corroborated Rodgers' account" during his appearance on ESPN. According to Pryor, "One source texted: 'It's all true.'" Anonymous team sources acknowledged Rodgers' claim that McCarthy fell asleep in meetings, according to The Athletic.

With that said, Rodgers did violate "the sanctity of the NFL locker room," as Tom Brady mentioned during his broadcast of the Thanksgiving matchup between the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys. One of the best quarterbacks in NFL history dropped a grenade in his building and walked away.

“Nobody wins when the family feuds.”@TomBrady on Aaron Rodgers pic.twitter.com/qLtmKL5oif

The Steelers locker room was expectedly mum on the situation, but quarterback Drew Allar did say it was "kinda sad to see," because of the respect he has for Rodgers.

There were plenty of others that did not hold their tongues, however. Former Packers offensive lineman T.J. Lang alleged Rodgers was a hypocrite for blacklisting players for telling the truth at other times, then going scorched-earth this week. Lang even said he's in a group chat with "a whole lot of former teammates" that feel the exact same way that he does.

"I think it's despicable," Lang said on 97.1 The Ticket in Detroit. "I think that Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has bitched about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media. He has blacklisted, I don't know how many former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth because he just he was sick of it."

TJ Lang on his former teammate Aaron Rodgers pic.twitter.com/0oiS3PybCn

Former Packers receiver and teammate James Jones said something very similar.

"How do you jump on Pat McAfee's show and say all this? Come on, man," Jones said on the Speakeasy podcast. "My text thread is full of texts and group chats with a lot of my teammates right now, and none are on 12's side, especially the ones that know Mike."

Another former Packers wideout in Greg Jennings chimed in on "First Things First," saying he was surprised by a lot of Rodgers' comments, and called his decision to air out this dirty laundry "distasteful."

"If you truly cared about more than just yourself, then you don't do this to everybody in that locker room that you just called brothers," Jennings said. "They are playing for something. You are no longer playing for anything."

@GregJennings weighs in on Steelers releasing former teammate Aaron Rodgers:“It was very distasteful… If you truly cared about more than just yourself, then you don’t do this to everybody in that locker room that you just called brothers... They are playing for something.” pic.twitter.com/whPyBO7K2p

Steelers president Art Rooney II released a statement on Thursday saying he stands behind McCarthy despite Rodgers' criticisms.

"I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he'll be our coach this season, next season and beyond," Rooney told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. "The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can't live with that."

Bears-Lions, Eagles-Cowboys and Chiefs-Bills all came down to the wire, allowing no time for a post-Thanksgiving nap.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more for Week 12.

Humphrey, who has spent his entire 10-year career in Baltimore, acknowledged the comments with an apology.

Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Brandon Aiyuk won't play this week after joining the team in practice on Friday for the first time.

Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland is considered week-to-week with a knee injury, the team announced on Friday.

Loveland is reportedly going for a second opinion on the injury, which was suffered during Thursday's 39-35 Thanksgiving Day win over the Detroit Lions. He is expected to miss time with what is reportedly a knee sprain, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Brown is dealing with a hamstring issue in an injury-riddled season that has limited him to just four games. He has played just once since Week 7.
